title: Giant Multiloculated Cystic Trochlear Nerve Schwannoma Between the Tentorial Leaflets: Case Report and Systematic Review.
abstract: Background Trochlear nerve schwannomas (TNSs) are exceptionally rare benign tumors, accounting for a very small fraction of intracranial schwannomas. Due to their deep locations and slow growth, they often reach a considerable size before diagnosis. Giant or multiloculated cystic variants are exceptionally uncommon and present significant diagnostic and surgical challenges. Methods A 32-year-old female presented with headache and dizziness but no diplopia. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed a giant multiloculated cystic lesion extending from the posterior fossa to the right temporal lobe, causing obstructive hydrocephalus. The mass was removed through a right paramedian supracerebellar transtentorial approach under intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring. The tumor was confined between the two tentorium leaflets with the trochlear nerve entering and exiting the lesion. Gross total resection was achieved with an uneventful postoperative course. Histopathology confirmed a World Health Organization Grade I schwannoma with Antoni A-B architecture and diffuse S-100 positivity. A systematic literature review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA 2020) guidelines, identifying forty-six surgically treated cases, analyzed together with the present case (n = 46). Results Mean age was 44.7 years with an approximately equal sex distribution. Most tumors (76.1%) were located in the ambient or crural cisterns, followed by the quadrigeminal cistern (10.8%) and cisterno-cavernous region (8.7%). Diplopia and trochlear nerve palsy were the most common presenting symptoms. Gross total resection was achieved in 80.4% of patients, while postoperative trochlear palsy occurred in 60.8%. No malignant transformation or early recurrence was reported. Conclusion This case represents one of the largest TNSs described and the second known lesion arising between the tentorial leaflets. Awareness of this unique anatomic configuration is essential for accurate preoperative diagnosis and surgical planning. A meticulous, anatomy-guided microsurgical approach enables complete resection while preserving neurological function in select cases.

title: Neurological prognostication after cardiac arrest: evidence review and institutional protocol proposal.
abstract: Background Cardiac arrest (CA) is associated with high mortality and neurological morbidity, mainly due to hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy. Accurate neurological prognostication in CA survivors is essential to guide therapeutic decisions and provide appropriate care. Objective To review the current evidence on neurological prognostication after CA and to propose an institutional protocol adapted to the resources of Hospital de Clínicas de Porto Alegre (HCPA). Methods The current narrative review was conducted in two stages: a literature review and the development of an institutional protocol. Articles were selected according to their clinical relevance and their contribution to current evidence on neurological prognostication after CA. The PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and SciELO databases were searched. The protocol was developed considering the clinical tools available at HCPA, including neurological examination, electroencephalography (EEG), and neuroimaging. Results Brain injury after CA occurs in three stages: intra-arrest ischemia, immediate reperfusion, and delayed postreperfusion injury. Prognostic modalities include neurological examination, EEG, somatosensory-evoked potentials (SSEPs), serum biomarkers, and neuroimaging. Reliable predictors of poor outcome include absent brainstem reflexes at 72 hours, persistent EEG suppression, bilateral absence of cortical N20 potentials, and diffuse abnormalities on magnetic resonance imaging. The proposed protocol organizes assessments from admission to the Intensive Care Unit through day 5 after the return of spontaneous circulation. Conclusion A standardized post-CA neurological prognostication protocol at HCPA may improve care quality, enhance communication with families, and support ethically-sound decision-making.

title: Automated Detection and Segmentation of Dental Caries in Panoramic Radiographs Using YOLOv8-Based Deep Learning Model.
abstract: Objectives This study aimed to develop an automated dental caries localization system through detection and classification using a deep learning (DL) approach based on You Only Look Once Version 8 (YOLOv8). Materials and methods YOLOv8 models were developed using 750 panoramic radiographs, which were divided into training, validation, and test sets at a ratio of 80%:10%:10%. The training and validation data were cropped into six regions to enhance the detection model performance. Confusion matrices were utilized to assess performance metrics, including accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1 score. Statistical analysis Fleiss's kappa was used to evaluate overall agreement among the YOLOv8 predictions and the expert evaluations, followed by Cohen's kappa for each comparison category. Results For caries detection, the YOLOv8-M model achieved an optimal accuracy of 95.22%, a sensitivity of 84.07%, a specificity of 98.18%, a precision of 92.46%, and an F1 score of 88.06%. For segmentation, the YOLOv8-X model achieved an optimal accuracy of 93.92%, a sensitivity of 78.30%, a specificity of 98.01%, a precision of 91.15%, and an F1 score of 84.24%. Fleiss's kappa analysis indicated substantial agreement of 0.766 ( p < 0.001) between model predictions and expert evaluations. Conclusion The YOLOv8 models demonstrated strong performance in detecting and segmenting dental caries in panoramic radiographs. They also showed substantial agreement with expert assessments, highlighting their potential as a reliable tool for automated caries identification. Further development is recommended to enhance performance, particularly by reducing false positive and false negative cases.

title: Legal and Regulatory Considerations for Artificial Intelligence Use in Medical and Radiology Research.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into medical imaging and radiology research, improving image acquisition, interpretation, workflow efficiency, and decision support. However, its rapid adoption has introduced complex legal and regulatory challenges involving patient privacy, data governance, algorithm validation, liability, intellectual property, transparency, cybersecurity, and ethical oversight. A comprehensive understanding of the evolving legal landscape is essential for the safe, effective, and legally compliant implementation of AI in radiology. A narrative review of the published literature and current regulatory guidance was conducted. Relevant international legal and regulatory frameworks governing AI in medical imaging were evaluated, including the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act, General Data Protection Regulation, U.S. Food and Drug Administration guidance on Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, World Health Organization recommendations, International Medical Device Regulators Forum principles, and selected national regulations. Key topics reviewed included data protection, informed consent, AI validation, regulatory approval pathways, post-market surveillance, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, explainability, and medico-legal responsibility. Current regulatory frameworks increasingly classify AI-enabled radiology software as SaMD, requiring risk-based evaluation, clinical validation, quality management systems, and continuous post-market performance monitoring. Regulatory authorities emphasize transparency, human oversight, data security, and lifecycle governance of AI systems. Nevertheless, important legal challenges remain, including liability for AI-assisted diagnostic errors, ownership of AI-generated outputs, secondary use of imaging data, cross-border data sharing, algorithmic bias, and regulation of adaptive or continuously learning AI models. The legal framework governing AI in radiology is evolving in parallel with technological innovation. Responsible integration of AI into clinical practice and research requires harmonized international regulations, robust data governance, standardized validation protocols, transparent algorithm development, and clearly defined legal accountability. Continued collaboration among radiologists, researchers, regulators, policymakers, industry, and legal experts will be essential to ensure that AI technologies remain safe, ethical, equitable, and trustworthy while maximizing their potential to improve patient care.

title: The role of thoracic interventional radiologists in the management of chest infections: a pictorial review.
abstract: Thoracic infections remain a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, requiring accurate and timely diagnosis to guide appropriate treatment. This pictorial review illustrates the role of the interventional thoracic radiologist in the management of infectious processes involving the lung, pleura, mediastinum, and chest wall. We describe a range of non-vascular image-guided percutaneous diagnostic and therapeutic techniques. These include targeted sampling for microbiological identification in complicated pneumonias and cavitary lesions, as well as image-guided drainage of pulmonary, pleural, mediastinal, and thoracic wall infectious collections. The advantages of these minimally invasive percutaneous techniques, especially in peripheral/subpleural lung lesions, are highlighted. In addition, we present practical technical considerations and diagnostic "tips and tricks," aimed at improving diagnostic yield. By integrating imaging findings with interventional strategies, this review underscores the growing clinical impact of interventional radiology in thoracic infections.

title: Vestibular manifestations as the initial presentation of multiple sclerosis: a case series.
abstract: Background Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic demyelinating disease of the central nervous system that can initially present with diverse neurological symptoms. Vestibular dysfunction may be an early manifestation, and can mimic common peripheral vestibular disorders, creating a diagnostic challenge. Objectives To characterize vestibular symptoms and clinical signs in patients with MS presenting initially with vestibular dysfunction. Materials and methods This retrospective observational case series included ten patients evaluated between 2019 and 2024 whose first clinical manifestation of MS was vestibular dysfunction. Clinical and neuro-otologic assessment, vHIT, and VNG were performed, and brain MRI was obtained when central vestibular involvement was suspected. Results Four main presentations were identified: acute vestibular syndrome ( n = 2), imbalance ( n = 4), recurrent vertigo ( n = 2), and positional vertigo ( n = 2). Nine of ten patients had at least one finding suggestive of central vestibular involvement, whereas one patient had a normal vestibular examination. Brain MRI demonstrated lesions fulfilling the radiological criteria for MS in all ten patients. Conclusions Central vestibular signs in young adults presenting with vestibular symptoms should raise suspicion of an underlying central lesion and possible MS. Recognition of these signs, together with appropriate neuroimaging when clinically indicated, may facilitate earlier diagnosis during the clinically isolated syndrome stage.

title: Multimodal based Brain Tumor Classification using Clustered Federated Learning in Edge based IoT Network.
abstract: A brain tumor is characterized by the uncontrolled growth of cells that causes a severe impact on the quality of life. Nowadays, various methods based on multimodal medical images are used to identify brain tumors. Meanwhile, these methods require extensive amounts of labeled information to identify disease tissues and often encounter various challenges based on privacy and accuracy. This paper establishes a Taylor-based Focal Log-cosh Entropy Network (TFLE-Net) to classify brain tumors from demographic data and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) images by utilizing clustered federated learning in an edge-based Internet of Things (IoT) network. The detection process is executed in clustered federated learning concerning two entities: server and nodes. In a local training model, an input MRI scan is pre-processed, further brain tumor areas are segmented, and then, the mining of various features is performed. Simultaneously, the normalization of input demographic data is done, and the suitable features are selected using information gain. Further, the extracted features and chosen features are subjected to TFLE-Net to classify brain tumors. Additionally, the TFLE-Net yielded Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.057, Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.047, True Positive Rate (TPR) of 97.789%, and accuracy of 96.987%.

title: Benchmarking 3D U-Net variants for volumetric segmentation of the substantia nigra and brain ageing related analysis using 7T MRI.
abstract: Objective: Accurate segmentation of the substantia nigra (SN) is essential for assessing its structural integrity and volumetric changes in Parkinson's disease and brain aging. However, it remains challenging due to SN's small size, deep location, and low contrast on conventional MRI. This study benchmarked six U-Net variants baseline 3D U-Net, ResU-Net, SE-U-Net, Attention U-Net, U-Net++, and U-Net 3+ for SN segmentation using ultra-high-field 7 T MRI. Methods T1-weighted MP2RAGE images from the ATAG dataset (53 healthy subjects: 31 train, 7 validation and 15 test). title: Long-segment posterior spinal instrumentation with intracanal bone fragment compaction for indirect anterior column support: a single-arm feasibility study in high load-sharing classification score thoracolumbar burst fractures.
abstract: Background Thoracolumbar burst fractures with high Load Sharing Classification (LSC) scores are mechanically unstable and associated with severe vertebral comminution and failure risk after short-segment fixation. This study evaluated outcomes of long-segment posterior fixation combined with intracanal bone fragment compaction as an indirect means of supporting the anterior column. Methods This retrospective study analyzed prospectively collected data from 121 consecutive patients with unstable thoracolumbar burst fractures (T10-L2) and LSC scores >6. All patients underwent open long-segment posterior instrumentation, decompression, and compaction of retropulsed intracanal bone fragments. Radiological outcomes included Cobb angle, percentage of anterior height compression (PAHC), vertebral body compression ratio (VBCR), and spinal canal compromise. Neurological recovery was assessed using the American Spinal Injury Association (ASIA) scale, and functional outcomes using the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI). Results The cohort included 70 men and 51 women, with a mean age of 37.2 years and follow-up of 23.2 months. At final follow-up, 58.7% (95% CI 49.8-67.1%) achieved ASIA grade E. Significant improvements were observed in VBCR, PAHC, Cobb angle (15.6° to 7.9°; p = 0.008), and spinal canal compromise (65.2% to 8.7%; p < 0.001). Mean ODI improved from 59.4 to 8.4 ( p < 0.001). Conclusion Long-segment posterior fixation with intracanal bone fragment compaction was associated with favorable short- to mid-term neurological, functional, and radiological outcomes. Prospective comparative studies with CT-based fusion assessment, standardized safety reporting, and longer follow-up are required to confirm effectiveness and durability.

title: Impact of cerebral venous outflow on futile recanalization despite complete reperfusion following mechanical thrombectomy.
abstract: Background A substantial proportion of patients with acute ischemic stroke remain functionally dependent despite complete angiographic reperfusion (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction [mTICI] 3) after mechanical thrombectomy (MT). This mismatch, commonly termed futile recanalization, may reflect tissue-level hypoperfusion not captured by arterial reperfusion grading. We investigated whether cerebral venous outflow, assessed using the Cortical Vein Opacification Score (COVES), provides prognostic information beyond conventional clinical and arterial imaging variables. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 420 adults with anterior-circulation large-vessel occlusion who underwent MT between 2015-2025 and achieved mTICI 3 reperfusion. Venous outflow was graded on baseline computed tomography angiography using COVES. Futile recanalization was defined as a 90-day modified Rankin Scale score of 3-6. Independent associations with futile recanalization were evaluated using multivariable binary logistic regression. Results Futile recanalization occurred in 191 patients (45.5%). After adjustment for age, admission NIHSS, ASPECTS, total passes, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, previous stroke, and arterial collateral status, higher COVES remained independently associated with lower odds of futile recanalization (OR per 1-point increase, 0.649; 95% CI, 0.537-0.784; p < 0.001). Age (OR, 1.031; p = 0.005), admission NIHSS (OR, 1.091; p = 0.001), and total passes (OR, 1.538; p < 0.001) were independently associated with higher odds of futile recanalization. Arterial collateral status was not independently associated with outcome. COVES showed greater discrimination than admission NIHSS (AUC, 0.742 vs 0.624). Conclusions Baseline COVES was independently associated with 90-day functional outcome among patients achieving complete reperfusion after MT. COVES may serve as a complementary prognostic imaging marker rather than a treatment-selection tool. Prospective external validation is required.

title: Deep learning-based segmentation of non-perfused volume after magnetic resonance guided high-intensity focused ultrasound therapies: a retrospective evaluation on clinical patient data.
abstract: Introduction Non-perfused volume (NPV) is a key imaging biomarker for treatment efficacy in MR -guided high-intensity focused ultrasound (MR-HIFU). In uterine fibroids therapies, the NPV ratio is strongly associated with clinical outcomes and long-term efficacy. We developed and clinically evaluated a deep learning-based automatic NPV segmentation model to facilitate standardized and efficient post-treatment assessment. Materials and methods Contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MR images from 79 patients treated with MR-HIFU were retrospectively analyzed, with NPVs manually delineated as the reference. A 2D U-Net convolutional neural network was optimized using a Tversky loss function (α = 0.7) to prioritize volumetric robustness. Performance was evaluated using similarity metrics (Dice coefficient [DC], 95th percentile Hausdorff distance [HD95]) and clinically relevant measures, including Bland-Altman analysis of volumetric quantification error, precision, recall, slice-level missing rate, and processing time. Results In the independent test cohort ( n = 12), the model achieved a median DC of 0.900 (IQR: 0.841-0.920) and a median HD95 of 0.42 (IQR: 0.32-0.60) mm. Median absolute NPV quantification error was 4.3 mL (IQR: 2.6-8.4 mL), corresponding to a median relative error of 2.3% (IQR: -2.4% - 10.5%). Precision and recall were 0.909 (IQR: 0.843-0.940) and 0.912 (IQR: 0.881-0.931), respectively, with 2.8% of ground truth-positive slices missed. Average processing time per patient (∼384 slices) was 1-2 min. Conclusion The proposed 2D U-Net provides accurate and time-efficient automatic NPV segmentation. Quantitative and clinically oriented evaluation demonstrates reliable volumetric assessment with minimal slice-level omission, supporting integration into routine MR-HIFU treatment workflows.

title: Successful treatment of an aggressive vertebral haemangioma with radiofrequency ablation and laminectomy: a case report.
abstract: Background and importance Aggressive vertebral haemangiomas are rare, hypervascular spinal tumours that can extend beyond the vertebral body, causing spinal cord compression and neurological deficits. These lesions are particularly challenging to manage due to high intraoperative bleeding risk. Although treatments like embolisation, radiotherapy, and surgical decompression have been employed, each carries limitations. Radiofrequency ablation (RFA), commonly used in metastatic spine disease, offers a targeted approach to devascularise lesions prior to surgery and may reduce perioperative morbidity. Clinical presentation A 17-year-old female presented with a three-week history of ascending lower limb numbness, gait ataxia, and recurrent falls. Examination revealed right lower limb weakness and sensory loss up to T5/6. MRI demonstrated an aggressive haemangioma of the T3 vertebra with extension into posterior elements and dorsal epidural compression. Given progressive symptoms, she underwent transpedicular RFA using a thermocouple-guided probe, followed by cement vertebroplasty and laminectomy (T1-T3). Intraoperatively, the posterior tumour component was unexpectedly absent, supporting the hypothesis that it collapsed following devascularisation. Neurological recovery progressed with structured physiotherapy, and no recurrence was noted on two-year follow-up imaging. Histological analysis of resected tissue confirmed a benign but clinically aggressive cavernous haemangioma, with vascular necrosis and thrombosis suggesting post-ablation changes. No malignancy was identified. Conclusion This case illustrates the potential of targeted RFA as an adjunctive strategy in the surgical management of aggressive vertebral haemangiomas. Preoperative devascularisation appeared to induce collapse of the posterior soft tissue component, reducing surgical complexity and minimising blood loss. This approach may enhance the safety of spinal tumour resection and optimise functional outcomes in select patients.

title: Diagnostic utility of the HAS-GCA score versus other Southend Giant Cell Arteritis Probability Score-ultrasound prediction models in giant cell arteritis.
abstract: Objective The aim of this study was to validate the HAS-GCA score, a prediction model combining the Southend Giant Cell Arteritis Probability Score (SGCAPS) with ultrasonography (US) halo count, and compare its diagnostic utility with other prediction models combining SGCAPS with US scores for diagnosing giant cell arteritis (GCA). Method : Treatment-naïve patients with suspected GCA were prospectively included in an observational cohort and underwent clinical assessment, including temporal artery biopsy (TAB) and pretreatment US and [ 18 F]fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography/computed tomography. The clinical diagnosis was confirmed after 24 weeks. Baseline data were assessed to calculate SGCAPS. Three prediction models combining SGCAPS with US scores - halo score, OMERACT GCA ultrasound score (OGUS), and halo count - were applied to classify patients into low-, intermediate-, and high-probability categories of GCA. The ability of the prediction models to correctly classify patients into low- and high-probability categories, and the proportion of patients with intermediate probability requiring additional tests, were compared. Results : GCA diagnosis was confirmed in 60/99 patients (61%). Prediction models based on halo count (HAS-GCA score), halo score, and OGUS had similar misclassification rates of 3%; HAS-GCA score had the lowest proportion of patients with intermediate probability (39% vs 47% and 59%, respectively). Conclusion : The HAS-GCA prediction model reliably stratified patients with suspected GCA into low- and high-probability categories, enabling confidence in ruling in or ruling out the GCA diagnosis. However, almost half of the patients required further evaluation to establish a correct diagnosis.

title: Differential diagnostic value of PAX1 and JAM3 methylation for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia between premenopausal and postmenopausal women: a retrospective clinical study in China.
abstract: PAX1/JAM3 methylation are promising biomarkers for high-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) detection, but menopausal status may affect diagnostic accuracy. This retrospective study compared their clinical performance between premenopausal and postmenopausal women undergoing colposcopy. 705 women undergoing colposcopy for abnormal screening results and/or clinical symptoms were stratified by menopausal status, including 192 postmenopausal and 513 premenopausal women. Subjects were further classified into ≤CIN1 and CIN2+ groups according to histopathology. Diagnostic and triage utility of PAX1/JAM3 methylation for identifying CIN2+ lesions were compared between premenopausal and postmenopausal women. PAX1/JAM3 methylation demonstrated superior diagnostic performance for CIN2+ detection in postmenopausal women compared with premenopausal women, either alone or in combination. Sensitivities of PAX1m and JAM3m in postmenopausal women (90.00%, 95% CI: 76.34-97.21%; 82.50%, 95% CI: 67.22-92.66%) were higher than those in premenopausal women (61.98%, 95% CI: 52.71-70.65%; 60.33%, 95% CI: 51.04-69.11%) (all p < 0.05). The combination improved sensitivity to 72.73% in premenopausal women and maintained 92.50% in postmenopausal women. Besides, PAX1/JAM3 methylation outperformed cytology and HPV16/18 testing in both groups (p < 0.001). In HPV16/18-positive or cytology triage, methylation increased positive predictive values (PPVs) for CIN2+/CIN3+ and reduced colposcopy referrals . However, CIN2+ missed rates in premenopausal women (27.54% for HPV16/18-positive triage and 23.85% for cytology triage) were higher than those in postmenopausal counterparts. The diagnostic performance of PAX1/JAM3 methylation for high-grade cervical lesions differs distinctly between premenopausal and postmenopausal women undergoing colposcopy. Menopausal status should be considered when applying methylation biomarkers, particularly as a valuable auxiliary tool to improve diagnostic accuracy in elderly women.

title: Temporal trends in incidence, clinical characteristics and outcomes of pyogenic vertebral osteomyelitis in Southern Denmark from 2009 to 2022: a retrospective population-based cohort study.
abstract: Objectives Pyogenic vertebral osteomyelitis (PVO) is a severe infection with increasing incidence. We aimed to describe long-term population-based temporal trends in incidence, clinical presentation, diagnostic approaches, microbiology, and outcomes. Materials and methods We conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study including 1,017 adults with multidisciplinary team-verified PVO diagnosed at a tertiary infectious diseases referral centre in the Region of Southern Denmark between 2009 and 2022. Incidence rates (IRs) per 100,000 person-years (PY) were calculated using regional population data and compared across three calendar periods (2009-2013, 2014-2018, 2019-2022). Temporal changes in clinical characteristics, microbiology, diagnostic strategies, and outcomes were assessed. Results In total, 1,017 patients were included. The crude IR increased from 4.7 per 100,000 PY in 2009-2013 to 11.0 in 2019-2022, with the largest increase among patients aged ≥70 years. Mean age and comorbidity burden rose over time. Pain was common, fever was often absent, and neurological deficits occurred in 33.5% ( n = 341). Postsurgical infection was the most frequent primary focus, and concomitant endocarditis occurred in 8.3% ( n = 84). A microbiological diagnosis was established in 64.8% ( n = 635) of cases, most commonly Staphylococcus aureus . Use of Fluorine-18 Fluorodeoxyglucose Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography ([ 18 F]FDG-PET/CT) increased over time. Median hospital stay remained 33 days. One-year mortality increased from 9.5% to 18.2%, while relapse declined, resulting in a stable composite risk of death or relapse (20.7%). Conclusions The incidence of PVO increased markedly from 2009 to 2022, predominantly in older patients with comorbidities. Despite improved diagnostics, microbiologically-negative cases remain frequent. Mortality remained high and increased over time.

title: Clinical Spectrum and Insights from One Year of Ocular Genetics at a Single Tertiary Eye Care Centre.
abstract: Introduction Genetic testing benefits individuals and families with inherited eye diseases by facilitating accurate diagnosis, informing prognosis, enabling assessment for at-risk family members, and supporting targeted therapies. This study aimed to characterize the spectrum of inherited eye disorders and evaluate the diagnostic yield of genetic testing at a single tertiary eye care centre over a one-year period. Methods A retrospective review of patients attending the ocular genetics service at a tertiary eye care centre in India from January 1 to December 31, 2024, was conducted. Results Of 1325 patients evaluated, 862 (65%) underwent genetic testing. Inherited retinal disorders were the most common ( n = 440, 51%), followed by cornea and anterior segment disorders ( n = 107, 12.4%). Other conditions included hereditary optic nerve disorders ( n = 75, 8.7%), glaucoma ( n = 70, 8.1%), lenticular disorders ( n = 54, 6.3%), phacomatoses ( n = 25, 2.9%), ocular tumours ( n = 20, 2.3%), strabismus and albinism ( n = 19 and 18; ~2% each), MAC spectrum disorders ( n = 10, 1.4%), and systemic syndromes ( n = 22, 2.5%). Diagnostic yield was achieved in 605 (70%), while 257 (30%) remained inconclusive. Of the 463 untested families, the motivations were unascertained reasons ( n = 156, 33%), financial constraints ( n = 138, 30%), intent to test later ( n = 90, 19%), and belief that no treatment was available ( n = 79, 17%). Discussion Inherited retinal and anterior segment disorders constitute the most frequent genetic eye diseases. Genetic testing has enabled genotype-phenotype correlation in over two-thirds of cases. Financial constraints and limited availability of disease-modifying treatments remain key barriers for uptake of genetic testing.

title: Ultrasound-Guided Dorsal Penile Nerve Block Reduces Perioperative Opioid Requirements in Pediatric Circumcision: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Aim This meta-analysis compares ultrasound-guided and landmark-based dorsal penile nerve block (DPNB) in pediatric circumcision. Methods We systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL from inception to December 2025. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational cohorts comparing ultrasound-guided with landmark-based DPNB in pediatric patients (≤18 years) undergoing circumcision. Primary outcomes were intraoperative and postoperative opioid rescue requirements. Secondary outcomes included pain scores at incision, surgical duration, discharge time, and postoperative nausea/vomiting. Meta-analyses were performed using RStudio version 4.4.3. Results Nine studies involving 949 children met inclusion criteria (five RCTs, four retrospective cohorts). Ultrasound-guided DPNB significantly reduced intraoperative opioid rescue (risk ratio 0.39, 0.18-0.88; p = 0.028) and postoperative opioid requirements (risk ratio 0.26, 0.07-0.94; p = 0.0442) compared with landmark-based techniques. No significant differences emerged in pain scores at incision, discharge time, or postoperative nausea/vomiting. Ultrasound-guided blocks required modestly longer procedural time (mean difference 1.48 min, 0.03-2.94; p = 0.048). Conclusions Ultrasound-guided DPNB substantially may reduce perioperative opioid requirements in pediatric circumcision compared with landmark-based approaches, despite slightly longer procedural times. When resources and expertise permit, ultrasound guidance should be considered the technique of choice for optimizing opioid-sparing anesthesia in this population.

title: Preparation and evaluation of degradable imaging drug loaded embolization microspheres for hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) necessitates the use of embolic agents with intrinsic radiopacity and controlled biodegradability to enhance therapeutic precision. In addressing the limitations inherent in current drug-eluting microspheres (DEMs), this study introduces the development of inherently radiopaque and biodegradable (DOX+Lipiodol) @PLGA @CaCO 3 @Alg core-shell microspheres. These microspheres were synthesized using rotating membrane emulsification and surface-induced ion crosslinking, with calcium carbonate serving multiple roles: a solid surfactant for Pickering stabilization, an acid-neutralizing agent, and an alginate shell inducer. The microspheres successfully encapsulated iodine loads, demonstrated by CT values reaching up to 8,000 HU, and contained doxorubicin at 1.53 ± 0.12 wt.%. They exhibited prolonged radiopacity for over 14 days in vivo and showed a pH-responsive drug release pattern, releasing 90% of their payload at pH 5.2 compared to 30% at pH 7.2 over 120 h. The sequential degradation process (alginate → CaCO 3 → PLGA) resulted in greater than 60% mass loss within four months, correlating with a reduction in CT attenuation. In rabbit embolization models, the microspheres achieved effective vascular occlusion and induced ischemic necrosis in ears and kidneys. CT tracking was possible without additional contrast agents, and systemic biosafety was confirmed with cell viability exceeding 90%, hemolysis below 1%, and normal hematological and histological profiles. These findings suggest that the microspheres could serve as a clinically translatable platform for image-guided TACE, integrating occlusion, therapy, and monitoring into a cohesive treatment strategy.

title: Clinical Features, Multimodal Imaging, and Neurological Differential Diagnoses in Recurrent Susac Syndrome.
abstract: Background Susac's syndrome (SuS) is a rare microangiopathy, often consisting of a classic, pathognomonic, clinical triad of sensorineural hearing impairment, encephalopathy, and retinal arterial occlusions. The variable presentation of SuS leads to underdiagnosis, despite the syndrome standing as an important differential in a variety of ophthalmic, neurological, and psychiatric presentations. Low case numbers and a fast progressive clinical course add to the difficulty of early recognition and treatment. Methods We report on a case of Susac's syndrome in a 40-year-old woman with the classic clinical triad. We report multimodal imaging findings in a patient with recurrent Susac syndrome and discuss these findings in the context of the existing literature. Particular emphasis is placed on neurological differential diagnosis, especially differentiation from multiple sclerosis and other causes of retinal vascular occlusion with nervous system involvement.We summarise the literature of other conditions that can present with retinal vascular occlusion, their associated central nervous system involvement, and imaging changes. Results Multimodal imaging demonstrated branch retinal artery occlusion (BRAO) with corresponding retinal ischaemic changes on optical coherence tomography (OCT) and optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), together with characteristic corpus callosal lesions on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The combination of retinal vascular occlusion and central corpus callosal involvement is useful in distinguishing Susac syndrome from important neurological differentials such as multiple sclerosis. Conclusions This case illustrates an example of how combined ophthalmic and neuroimaging findings may support recognition of recurrent Susac syndrome and facilitate distinction from other neurological disorders presenting with retinal vascular occlusion, particularly multiple sclerosis.

title: Multimodal Imaging Characteristics of Sarcoid Retinal Granulomas.
abstract: Purpose To describe the clinical presentation and multimodal imaging characteristics of retinal granulomas in patients with ocular sarcoidosis. Methods In this retrospective observational case series, patients with definite or presumed ocular sarcoidosis presenting with retinal granulomas were evaluated. Multimodal retinal imaging was reviewed to characterize lesion morphology, imaging patterns, and longitudinal evolution. Results Retinal granulomas were identified in three patients with ocular sarcoidosis from diverse racial backgrounds. On fundus photographs, lesions ranged from multiple, superficial, small, faint yellow-gray nodules to more distinct, deeper yellow lesions, predominantly located in the mid- to peripheral retina. All retinal granulomas demonstrated hyperreflectivity on OCT with four distinct morphologic patterns: (1) inner and/or outer retinal granulomas; (2) retinal granulomas associated with retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) disruption and hypertransmission defects; (3) sub-RPE granulomas located between the RPE and Bruch's membrane; and (4) combined chorioretinal granulomas extending from the choroid. FAF demonstrated predominantly isoautofluorescent lesions in the absence of RPE involvement, whereas hypoautofluorescence was observed when the RPE was involved. FA was available for one patient and demonstrated late hyperfluorescent staining of the retinal granulomas. Longitudinal imaging demonstrated evolution from active inflammatory nodules to regression with residual retinal and/or RPE changes, commonly manifesting as punched-out atrophic lesions. Conclusion Retinal granulomas may represent an underrecognized manifestation of ocular sarcoidosis. In our series, multimodal imaging allowed detailed characterization of their morphologic patterns and longitudinal evolution. Recognition of these characteristic imaging features of sarcoid retinal granulomas may facilitate consideration of sarcoidosis in the differential diagnosis of retinal infiltrative lesions.

title: Diagnostic Performance of Deep Learning Models for Ocular Toxoplasmosis Using Fundus Photography: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Background Ocular toxoplasmosis (OT) is the leading infectious cause of posterior uveitis worldwide, yet diagnosis remains challenging without a universal gold standard. Although deep learning (DL) shows significant promise for automated image analysis, a rigorous synthesis of its diagnostic accuracy across heterogeneous architectures and datasets is lacking. Methods Following PRISMA-DTA and CLAIM-AI guidelines, we searched major databases through January 2026 for studies evaluating DL models for OT detection using fundus photography. Methodological quality was appraised using QUADAS-2. A bivariate random-effects model (MetaDTA v2.1.3) was applied to pool sensitivity and specificity, generating hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) curves to visualize discriminatory performance. Results Sixteen primary studies (38 model configurations) met qualitative synthesis criteria; nine studies evaluating 24 unique architectures provided sufficient 2×2 contingency data for meta-analysis. Pooled sensitivity was 0.965 (95% CI: 0.944-0.978) and pooled specificity was 0.955 (95% CI: 0.929-0.972). The diagnostic odds ratio reached 594.1 (95% CI: 263.3-1340.4), with positive and negative likelihood ratios of 21.6 and 0.036. Substantial between-study heterogeneity was observed (I^2 = 87.9%). Critically, 81.2% of included studies relied exclusively on a single Paraguayan dataset (OTFID), raising concerns regarding phenotypic bias and limited global generalizability. Conclusion DL models demonstrate excellent diagnostic accuracy for OT on fundus photography, comparable to established ophthalmic AI benchmarks. However, clinical translation is constrained by geographic data homogeneity and the absence of multicentric external validation. Future research must prioritize diverse international cohorts, explainable AI, and federated learning frameworks.

title: Posterior Scleritis Following Uneventful Small-Incision Cataract Surgery.
abstract: Background Posterior scleritis following routine, uncomplicated cataract surgery in a patient without underlying systemic disease is an exceedingly rare and potentially sight-threatening clinical entity. Method A 55-year-old female with no systemic medical history presented three weeks after uneventful small-incision cataract surgery (SICS) in the right eye with sudden vision loss, redness, and severe ocular pain exacerbated by eye movements. Her best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) had deteriorated from 6/9 to finger counting close to her face. Dilated fundus examination revealed multiple dull yellow subretinal lesions across the posterior pole. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showed hyperreflective vitreous cells, subretinal fluid (SRF), and choroidal undulations. B-scan ultrasonography confirmed diffuse posterior scleritis, demonstrating localized sclerochoroidal thickening and fluid accumulation in the sub-Tenon's space. Comprehensive laboratory testing and imaging ruled out infectious and autoimmune etiologies. Result The patient was treated with high-dose intravenous pulse methylprednisolone (1 g/day for three days) followed by an oral prednisolone taper, which led to immediate pain relief and anatomical resolution. At six months, the scleritis had completely resolved with a BCVA improvement to 6/12, limited by persistent localized disruption of the foveal ellipsoid zone on OCT. The patient remained recurrence-free at six months. Conclusion Diffuse posterior scleritis can occur as a postoperative inflammatory phenomenon following uneventful cataract surgery. Clinicians must maintain a high index of suspicion, utilize B-scan ultrasonography for diagnosis, and initiate prompt systemic corticosteroid therapy to optimize anatomical and visual outcomes.

title: Quantitative assessment of cervical spinal cord injury: Methods, clinical utility, and future directions.
abstract: Study design Literature review. Objectives To provide a structured narrative summary of quantitative assessment methods for cervical spinal cord injury (SCI), analyze their stage-specific applicability, discuss limitations, and clarify the clinical utility and future integration of wearable sensors and artificial intelligence (AI). Methods A narrative review was conducted using PubMed, Web of Science, and EBSCO to identify English-language, peer-reviewed studies published between 1967 and 2026 on quantitative assessment of traumatic and non-traumatic cervical SCI. The search covered imaging, neurological and functional evaluation, electrophysiology, biomechanics, wearable monitoring, artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer vision, and multimodal data integration. An updated PubMed search performed on May 15, 2026 identified 1,042 records. After title and abstract screening, 873 records were retained as potentially relevant, and 73 unique publications were included in the final narrative synthesis following full-text review and deduplication. Results Main methods include imaging (CT, MRI/DTI, AI-image analysis), neurological scales (ASIA/ISNCSCI, SCIM, WISCI), neuroelectrophysiology (SSEP, MEP, EMG), biomechanics (sEMG and kinematics), and wearable sensors. These methods provide complementary structural, neurological, functional, and real-world activity information across acute care, rehabilitation, and long-term follow-up. Current approaches remain limited by subjectivity, poor real-time monitoring, limited quantification precision, equipment dependence, and insensitivity to early or subclinical changes. Wearable-AI integration may improve continuous monitoring, risk prediction, pressure injury prevention, and the selection of patients who may benefit from transcutaneous or epidural stimulation. Conclusion Current quantitative assessment methods for cervical SCI are insufficient when used alone. A staged, multimodal strategy that combines conventional clinical assessment with wearable sensing and AI-supported analysis may improve full-process management, clinical decision-making, and prognostic assessment in cervical SCI.

title: Racial residential segregation and receipt of breast cancer screening in the United States: a national cross-sectional study, 2020.
abstract: Objectives Breast cancer is the most common cancer among the U.S. women, with a lifetime risk that exceeds 13%. In 2026, it is projected that approximately 321,910 new cases of invasive breast cancer will be diagnosed. While there are many well-known barriers to breast cancer screening, the effect of residential segregation on access to screening services is not fully understood. Design This study utilized data from the 2020 U.S. Health Information National Trends Survey Data Linkage Project (HDLP2020) for 1329 women aged 40-75 years. Fitting generalized linear models with the maximum likelihood estimation, we explored the relationship between residential segregation and mammography screening rates. Secondary analyses examined the role of race (White vs. non-White) and rural-urban status in these associations. Results Women in higher residential segregation were less likely to have undergone mammography in the past year, relative to those in less segregated areas (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 0.40; 95% CI: 0.16-0.97; p -value = 0.04). Non-White women in moderately segregated regions also exhibited lower screening rates than those in low-segregation areas. Additionally, women in highly segregated urban settings were less likely to report mammography screening than their counterparts in less segregated urban areas (adjusted OR = 0.39; 95% CI: 0.16-0.92; p -value = 0.03). Conclusion The findings demonstrate that in more racially segregated communities, women are less likely to receive screening mammograms, particularly those who are non-White and live in urban settings. Efforts to improve breast cancer screening may account for the contextual and community determinants of health and address the specific needs of women in moderately to highly segregated areas to potentially reduce disparities and promote health equity.

title: Late onset retinoblastoma in a child with 13 q deletion syndrome.
abstract: A nine-year-old boy presented with right leukocoria, prompting an ophthalmic evaluation that revealed an exophytic group E retinoblastoma. Initial systemic assessment revealed intellectual disability and dysmorphic facies. Conventional cytogenetic analysis of peripheral blood lymphocytes revealed male karyotype (46, XY). Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) using a locus-specific probe targeting the RB1 gene at chromosome 13q14 demonstrated a deletion in approximately 90% of interphase nuclei and consequently the diagnosis of 13 q deletion was established. Chromosomal microarray identified a ~ 20-Mb deletion at 13q13.3-q21.1 (×1) and a ~ 20-Mb duplication at 13q21.31-q31.1 (×3). MRI orbit and brain showed no optic nerve or intracranial extension. Metastatic work up including CSF sample and BM aspirates was free. Due to advanced group E retinoblastoma, the decision was to perform enucleation. Subsequent histopathological examination revealed high risk features in the enucleated eye and the child received post enucleation chemotherapy. One year afterward, there are no detectable recurrences. To our knowledge, this represents one of the oldest reported cases of retinoblastoma in association with 13q deletion syndrome.

title: Cost-effectiveness of RIMS1 methylation-guided gastric cancer surveillance after Helicobacter pylori eradication.
abstract: Background The cost-effectiveness of methylation-guided surveillance after Helicobacter pylori eradication remains uncertain. Research design and methods From a healthcare system perspective, a cohort model compared annual, biennial, and RIMS1 methylation-guided surveillance over 30 years in Japanese patients aged 50 years with open-type gastric atrophy. Differences in stage at diagnosis were calibrated from annual-surveillance data. Costs and quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) were discounted at 3.0% annually. Sensitivity analyses examined uncertainty; an exploratory analysis used Korean inputs. Results At US$52,037.74/QALY, methylation-guided surveillance had the highest net monetary benefit (NMB). Compared with biennial surveillance, its incremental cost-effectiveness ratio was US$47,021.24/QALY and incremental NMB was US$62.56/person. It reduced routine endoscopies by 40.9% versus annual surveillance. Cost-effectiveness varied with surveillance duration, endoscopy-related utility loss, implementation costs, and risk misclassification. Across 5,000 probabilistic draws, methylation-guided surveillance had the highest mean NMB, but biennial surveillance was more often optimal (51.2% vs 36.0%). The preferred strategy in the Korean analysis varied with endoscopy costs. Conclusions In the base-case analysis, RIMS1-guided surveillance was cost-effective, increasing QALYs compared with biennial surveillance and reducing endoscopy use compared with annual surveillance. Its estimated cost-effectiveness depends on the assumed improvement in stage at diagnosis with more frequent surveillance.

title: Non-invasive neuromodulation after repetitive head impacts: current evidence and a precision framework for circuit-based rehabilitation.
abstract: Repetitive head impacts (RHIs) are associated with heterogeneous cognitive, behavioral, psychiatric, sleep-related, pain, and neurological symptoms. Chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) remains a postmortem neuropathological diagnosis, whereas traumatic encephalopathy syndrome (TES) is a clinical research syndrome assessed during life. No intervention has been shown to modify CTE pathology, but neuromodulation may support the surviving neural circuits. PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus and Google Scholar were searched from database inception to August 2026 for this narrative review. The author evaluates magnetic and electrical stimulation, low-intensity ultrasound, photobiomodulation and cranial nerve stimulation as adjuncts to rehabilitation after repetitive head impacts. Direct RHI/TES evidence is distinguished from findings in other traumatic brain injury and concussion populations, other clinical populations and experimental models. The author then proposes a phenotype- and circuit-guided framework for treatment development. Neuromodulation should not be considered a disease-modifying treatment for CTE. Its most credible role is as a phenotype-led adjunct to rehabilitation. This approach requires identification of a viable circuit relevant to the dominant impairment, selection of an individualized stimulation dose, measurement of target engagement and pairing with symptom-relevant rehabilitation. Progress requires credible sham-controlled and factorial trials, multimodal biomarkers, clinically meaningful functional outcomes, and long-term follow-up.

title: Clinical features associated with HFUS-defined vascular occlusion after hyaluronic acid facial injections: a retrospective exploratory study.
abstract: Hyaluronic acid (HA) filler injections are widely used in aesthetic treatments but can cause vascular occlusion. Early diagnosis is often delayed due to reliance on clinical experience. High-frequency ultrasound (HFUS) offers a noninvasive diagnostic method. The study aims to explore the association between clinical warning signs and HFUS-defined vascular occlusion after HA filler injections. This retrospective study analyzed 57 patients with suspected vascular occlusion after HA filler injections. HFUS and a clinical scoring system covering seven symptom categories were used for early evaluation. Occlusion and non-occlusion groups were compared using HFUS and clinical scores. Among 57 clinically suspected cases, 42 (73.7%) were classified as HFUS-defined vascular occlusion and 15 (26.3%) were classified as non-occlusion. In multivariable analysis, skin color change (OR 30.390, 95% CI: 2.482-372.039; p = .008) and delayed capillary refill time (OR 185.936, 95% CI: 2.638- 13,095.200; p = .016) were associated factors of vascular occlusion. A two-variable model incorporating there two features yielded an AUC of 0.944 (95% CI: 0.891-0.998). Skin color change and delayed capillary refill time were associated with HFUS-defined vascular occlusion in this exploratory cohort. These findings may help inform clinical assessment but require prospective validation in independent populations.

title: Post-treatment risks of transcatheter aortic valve implantation: should we be increasing preventative measures?
abstract: Introduction Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has become an established treatment for severe aortic stenosis across an expanding risk spectrum. As indications extend to younger and lower-risk patients, post-treatment complications with implications for survival, quality of life, and valve durability require attention. Areas covered This narrative review discusses major post-TAVI complications with direct implications for procedural planning and lifetime management, including cerebrovascular events, conduction abnormalities, coronary obstruction and aortic root injury, bioprosthetic valve dysfunction, valve thrombosis, residual regurgitation, and TAVI-associated infective endocarditis. Evidence was reviewed from pivotal randomized trials, contemporary registries, consensus documents, systematic reviews, and mechanistic studies addressing incidence, pathophysiology, predictors, prognosis, prevention, diagnosis, and management of these complications. Expert opinion Post-TAVI risk reduction should move beyond reactive complication management toward individualized prevention. Meticulous computed tomography-based planning, optimized valve selection and implantation technique, rational antithrombotic therapy, structured rhythm and valve surveillance, selective use of cerebral embolic protection, timely correction of clinically or hemodynamically significant residual regurgitation, and infection-prevention pathways are central components of contemporary care. Future progress will depend on better risk stratification, longer-term durability data, and targeted preventive strategies adapted to lower-risk patients with longer life expectancy.

title: Bone microarchitecture, density, and strength assessment in automotive trauma patients using HR-pQCT: a pilot study.
abstract: Objective Automotive trauma patients enrolled in the Crash Injury Research and Engineering Network (CIREN) typically undergo computed tomography (CT) imaging as part of emergency care. HR-pQCT is a noninvasive imaging technique that enables assessment of bone microarchitecture at the peripheral sites. CT and HR-pQCT can be used to estimate volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD) and strength via finite element analysis (FEA). However, HR-pQCT's superior resolution (approximately 10 times higher than conventional clinical CT scanners) captures in vivo trabecular and cortical microarchitecture, enabling high fidelity FEA. This study examines HR-pQCT-derived bone microarchitecture and strength measurements in relation to fracture patterns, bone-related comorbidities, and CT-derived vBMD in CIREN trauma patients, while providing foundational evidence to support HR-pQCT use following motor vehicle crashes (MVC) and pedestrian crashes. Methods Nine automotive trauma patients (ages 17-76; 78% female) enrolled at Atrium Health Wake Forest Baptist Medical Center from the National Highway Safety Administration's CIREN study participated in the HR-pQCT pilot study. HR-pQCT scans were acquired within 1-12 months following the patient's MVC ( n = 7) or pedestrian crash ( n = 2). Scans were acquired at four sites: 1) distal tibia, 2) diaphyseal tibia, 3) distal radius, and 4) diaphyseal radius. HR-pQCT normative percentiles were determined using Indiana University's calculator. Descriptive statistics were used to present HR-pQCT musculoskeletal outcomes based on bone-related comorbidities, BMI, and fracture incidence. Pearson correlations were performed between HR-pQCT-derived distal tibia and radius total vBMD and CT-derived total vBMD at the spine and femoral compartments. Results At the distal tibia, participants without tibia and fibula fractures tended to show greater mean cortical thickness (1.63 ± 0.38 versus 1.15 ± 0.05 mm), cortical area (146.24 ± 46.07 versus 103.70 ± 1.70 mm 2 ), cortical vBMD (943.83 ± 79.18 versus 861.05 ± 26.52 mg HA/cm 3 ), and bone strength (10.25 ± 3.72 versus 7.00 ± 0.70 kN). Additionally, HR-pQCT-derived distal tibia total vBMD demonstrated a strong positive correlation with CT-derived femoral head total vBMD ( r = 0.766; p = 0.045). Normative percentiles showed that participants with bone-related comorbidities had lower bone microarchitectural and strength percentiles than the group without comorbidities. Conclusion This study demonstrates the viability of HR-pQCT for characterizing bone microarchitecture, strength, and density in automotive trauma patients and identifying differences that might relate to fracture and bone-related comorbidities. These preliminary findings support incorporating HR-pQCT imaging into automotive crash research due to its ability to provide detailed cortical and trabecular microarchitectural measurements that are not available from clinical CT.

title: SSH1 knockdown increases autophagosome formation through ATG9A recruitment and promotes tau protein degradation.
abstract: Pathological accumulation of MAPT/tau protein is a defining feature of Alzheimer disease (AD) and related tauopathies, highlighting the need to identify druggable regulators of MAPT/tau clearance. Using Drosophila behavioral assays focused on cytoskeletal remodeling pathways dysregulated in AD, we identified genes whose genetic modulation mitigates MAPT/tau-induced behavioral deficits. These modifiers were validated by histopathology and mechanistically examined in human tauopathy cell models to determine their impact on autophagy-dependent MAPT/tau degradation. Autophagic flux, ATG9A trafficking, and autophagosome biogenesis were further analyzed. Across models, reduction of the phosphatase SSH1 consistently lowered steady-state MAPT/tau levels by enhancing autophagic flux through a mechanism distinct from its canonical regulation of CFL1. Mechanistically, SSH1 functions as a negative regulator of early autophagosome formation: SSH1 depletion promotes ATG9A mobilization to the endoplasmic reticulum-phagophore assembly site (ER-PAS), thereby accelerating autophagic vesicle biogenesis. Importantly, the MAPT/tau-lowering effect of Dmssh attenuation was abolished in flies haploinsufficient for DmAtg9, demonstrating that SSH1-mediated MAPT/tau clearance requires ATG9 function. Consistent with a direct regulatory interaction, in vitro phosphatase assays revealed that recombinant SSH1 decreases ATG9A phosphorylation in the presence of actin, identifying an SSH1-ATG9A regulatory axis controlling autophagosome initiation. These findings position SSH1 as a nodal inhibitor of autophagy initiation whose inhibition enhances MAPT/tau proteolysis. Notably, SSH1 haploinsufficiency also reduces SNCA/α-synuclein accumulation in vivo, indicating broader relevance to neurodegenerative proteopathies. By integrating in vivo functional screening with mechanistic studies in human cells, this work identifies SSH1 as a druggable phosphatase that constrains autophagy at the level of ATG9A-dependent vesicle formation.

title: An interpretable skin cancer detection and classification framework using meta-heuristic driven symmetric convolution-based adaptive MobileNet with LSTM layer.
abstract: Skin cancer requires early and accurate detection for effective treatment. Automated image analysis can help identify skin lesions and support clinical diagnosis.This study aims to develop an efficient framework for accurate skin cancer detection using lesion segmentation, deep learning, and optimization.Skin lesion images are first segmented using MobileUNet++ with Spatial Attention (MUNet++-SA) to identify lesion regions accurately. The segmented images are then classified using the proposed SAMNet-LSTM model. The model parameters are optimized using Rationalized Masterpiece Optimization (RMO) to improve classification performance. The proposed method is compared with existing approaches.The proposed MUNet++-SA achieves improved segmentation performance. Its mean IoU is 16.47%, 15.88%, 14.11%, and 8.23% higher than U-Net, U-Net3+, ResUNet, and DenseUNet, respectively. The RMO-optimized SAMNet-LSTM also provides improved and efficient skin cancer classification.The proposed framework combines accurate lesion segmentation with optimized deep learning for reliable skin cancer detection. It can support faster and more effective clinical decision-making.

title: Artificial intelligence in modern medicine: a comprehensive review of technologies, applications, and future directions.
abstract: We evaluated the transformative impact of AI modalities on clinical practice, distinguishing between retrospective algorithmic performance and prospective clinical effectiveness. Comprehensive searches were executed [databases searched: January 2016 to October 2024] across PubMed/Medline, Scopus, and Web of Science, identifying peer-reviewed original research and clinical trials. Non-peer-reviewed materials and commercial web sources were strictly excluded. AI technologies-particularly deep learning (DL), natural language processing (NLP), and foundation models-demonstrate high diagnostic accuracy in retrospective cohorts across radiology, dermatology, and pathology. In precision therapeutics, AI accelerates drug discovery and facilitates multi-omics integration for individualized treatment planning. Furthermore, autonomous AI systems have proven cost-effective in nationwide diabetic retinopathy screening programs. However, significant gaps remain between in-silico success and real-world clinical utility. Primary barriers include the lack of prospective randomized trials, pervasive risks of algorithmic bias threatening health equity, the "black box" nature of deep neural networks, and stringent interoperability challenges. AI serves as a potent computational catalyst for advancing personalized medicine. To transition from retrospective experimental success to standard-of-care clinical integration, future research endeavors must prioritize Explainable AI (XAI), federated learning frameworks for privacy preservation, and rigorous prospective clinical validation under standardized regulatory oversight.

title: Spinal neurocysticercosis: synthesizing evidence on clinical presentations, anatomical patterns, diagnostic approaches, and therapeutic strategies.
abstract: Spinal neurocysticercosis (NCC) is an uncommon manifestation of NCC involving the spinal cord, meninges, nerve roots, and subarachnoid spaces. Although less common than intracranial disease, spinal involvement can cause substantial neurological morbidity because even small lesions within the confined spinal canal may produce progressive myelopathy. Disease may result from hematogenous dissemination or cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) spread of Taenia solium larvae and may present as intramedullary, intradural extramedullary, subarachnoid, or, rarely, extradural lesions. Clinical manifestations are diverse and include paraparesis, quadriparesis, cauda equina syndrome, and chronic meningitis. Magnetic resonance imaging is the diagnostic modality of choice, providing detailed assessment of lesion location, evolutionary stage, inflammatory activity, and associated complications. CSF analysis and immunological or molecular tests provide supportive evidence, while histopathological examination confirms the diagnosis when tissue is available. Treatment is individualized and may include antiparasitic agents, corticosteroids, and surgery when indicated. Although outcomes are generally favorable with early diagnosis and appropriate treatment, delayed treatment, extensive arachnoiditis, diffuse leptomeningeal disease, and established spinal cord damage may result in permanent neurological deficits. Further prospective studies are needed to refine diagnostic strategies and optimize management. PubMed database was searched from inception to 13 July 2026, for spinal neurocysticercosis and spinal cysticercosis.

title: Clinical management and multimodal imaging features of brucellar mastitis mimicking metastatic breast carcinoma: a rare case report and literature review.
abstract: Brucella mastitis represents a rare infectious disease that is frequently misdiagnosed as metastatic breast carcinoma, particularly when older women present with systemic manifestations. Here, we report a 60-year-old woman presenting with a neck pain and left upper extremity numbness. Initial contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (CEMR) and 18 F -FDG PET-CT highly suggested breast malignancy with osseous metastasis, while contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) provided critical microvascular perfusion insights favoring an inflammatory process. The diagnosis was ultimately confirmed via blood culture and pathological examination. The patient was successfully treated with targeted antimicrobial treatment. This case offers important insights into the multimodal imaging differentiation of atypical breast lesions and emphasizes the diagnostic challenges of Brucella mastitis accompanied by systemic osteoarticular involvement.

title: Neuroimaging and neurophysiological changes following structured interventions in children with developmental coordination disorder: a scoping review.
abstract: Background Longitudinal neuroimaging and neurophysiological studies can indicate whether structured interventions in developmental coordination disorder (DCD) are accompanied by neurobiological change, but this literature has not been synthesized across modalities, follow-up intervals, and analytic approaches. Objective To map longitudinal neurobiological outcomes after structured interventions in children and adolescents with DCD or probable DCD and the analytic approaches used, including neurobiological-clinical/functional linkage analyses. Methods We conducted a scoping review following JBI methodology, reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR and PRISMA-S. Eligible sources included participants aged 0-18 years with confirmed or probable DCD, a structured intervention, and neurobiological assessment at baseline and ≥1 post-intervention time point. Two reviewers independently screened records and charted data. We searched six databases, two trial registries, and preprint platforms on January 10, 2026 (updated August 21, 2026), without date or language restrictions. Formal critical appraisal was not undertaken; methodological and reporting features were charted descriptively. Results Of 747 records identified, 13 sources (eight independent cohorts) published between 2012 and 2025 met the inclusion criteria. Neurobiological sample sizes ranged from 20 to 88 (median 49). Designs included randomized controlled, non-randomized controlled, and quasi-experimental pre-post studies. Interventions clustered into Cognitive Orientation to daily Occupational Performance (CO-OP; 6 sources), exercise/motor-learning programs (4), and neuromuscular/biomechanical approaches (3). Modalities included diffusion tensor imaging, resting-state functional MRI, structural MRI/voxel-based morphometry, functional near-infrared spectroscopy, electroencephalography/event-related potentials, and surface electromyography. MRI-based longitudinal outcomes were reported exclusively in CO-OP cohorts, with several publications arising from shared registered trials and partial cohort overlap. Six sources included neurobiological follow-up beyond the immediate post-intervention assessment. Analytic approaches varied in pre-post versus group-by-time contrasts, region-of-interest versus whole-brain analyses, and correction for multiple comparisons. Seven sources reported neurobiological-clinical/functional linkage analyses; five tested change-based associations, and statistically significant findings were limited to individualized movement-quality outcomes. Conclusions The evidence base is small, heterogeneous, and unevenly distributed across intervention categories and modalities. Priorities include independent replication, longitudinal neuroimaging of non-CO-OP interventions where scientifically justified, more consistent follow-up, and prespecified, adequately powered linkage analyses.

title: Atypical late neurosyphilis presenting as status epilepticus: diagnostic and screening implications.
abstract: Objectives Neurosyphilis is a serious complication of poorly treated syphilis due to Treponema pallidum invasion of the central nervous system. Symptoms vary from silent infection to severe neurological deficits. Despite progress in diagnostics and treatment, the diagnosis is frequently missed because it is not considered, particularly in atypical presentations and in patients with no evident risk factor. . Methods A 45-year-old man presented with confusion, speech difficulties, and left-sided weakness following subtle behavioral changes. In the emergency department, he had a witnessed focal-to-bilateral tonic-clonic seizure starting with head deviation to the left and tonic posturing of the left arm. Brain CT was normal, while MRI revealed right thalamic and bilateral temporal FLAIR hyperintensities with diffusion restriction in the thalamus. CSF showed mild pleocytosis (17 WBC/µL) and raised protein (67.6 mg/dL). Serum treponemal screening was positive with an RPR titre > 1:32. Neurosyphilis was confirmed by a reactive CSF non-treponemal test (RPR 1:2) in a patient with compatible clinical and CSF findings; the CSF TPHA titre was >1:10,240, which is supportive but not in itself a diagnostic criterion.Levetiracetam was started on admission and intravenous penicillin G on day 2, after the diagnosis was confirmed. Because EEG and MRI suggested possible focal status epilepticus, valproate and phenytoin were added. The patient developed respiratory failure needing mechanical ventilation and deep vein thrombosis. After extended ICU stay and rehabilitation, he recovered with mild residual critical illness myopathy and cognitive deficits. Conclusion Neurosyphilis is not intrinsically difficult to diagnose, provided it is considered, including outside the classically recognised risk groups such as men who have sex with men.

title: Childhood peer abuse moderates associations of inflammation and cortisol with subcortical brain volume.
abstract: Objective: Childhood peer abuse is a developmentally salient form of interpersonal adversity, yet its role in shaping links between peripheral biological stress markers and brain structure remains poorly understood. The present cross-sectional study examined whether retrospectively reported childhood peer verbal and physical abuse moderated associations of systemic inflammatory burden and hair cortisol with subcortical brain volume.Methods: Participants from a community sample completed the Maltreatment and Abuse Chronology of Exposure scale and structural magnetic resonance imaging. Inflammatory burden was indexed by a composite of standardised IL-6, IL-8, TNF-alpha, and C-reactive protein values (n = 292), and hair cortisol was available in a subsample (n = 172). Bilateral amygdala, hippocampus, putamen, and caudate volumes were extracted from FreeSurfer segmentation. Linear regression models adjusted for gender, age, parental education, and estimated total intracranial volume; false discovery rate correction was applied across the four ROI tests within each marker-by-moderator family.Results: Peer verbal abuse moderated associations of inflammatory burden with bilateral amygdala volume (β = -.095, pFDR = .032) and bilateral putamen volume (β = -.115, pFDR = .017). Peer physical abuse moderated the association between hair cortisol and bilateral amygdala volume (β = .227, pFDR = .035). Caudate models did not survive correction. Core findings remained significant after sensitivity adjustment for broader childhood adversity and current depression/anxiety symptoms.Conclusions: Associations differed across brain regions, biological markers, and peer-abuse subtypes. These findings identify peer adversity as an important interpersonal context for understanding stress-related brain differences.

title: Early extracranial dissemination with prolonged survival in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma: case study and comprehensive literature review.
abstract: Background Extracranial metastasis of glioblastoma (GBM) is rare (0.4-2%) and associated with poor prognosis. For this report, "early extracranial dissemination" is defined as radiographically and histologically confirmed metastatic disease identified at or within one month of the index GBM diagnosis, distinguishing it from metastasis arising later in the disease course. Case presentation A 65-year-old woman with IDH-wildtype, MGMT-methylated GBM presented with seizures, right hemiplegia, and expressive aphasia. She underwent near-total resection followed by chemoradiotherapy with temozolomide. A suspicious right lower lobe pulmonary lesion was identified on initial staging, and biopsy-confirmed GBM involving mediastinal lymph nodes was established within one month of diagnosis. Despite pulmonary and mediastinal involvement, intracranial hemorrhage, seizures, and venous thromboembolism, she survived 25 months from diagnosis and 24 months following confirmation of metastatic disease. Discussion This case is notable for exceptionally early extracranial dissemination, pulmonary and mediastinal involvement, and prolonged post-metastatic survival. MGMT methylation and sustained temozolomide therapy may have contributed to disease control, although these observations remain hypothesis-generating. Conclusion Early extracranial dissemination may be underrecognized and warrants further investigation through risk-stratified approaches to extracranial surveillance.

title: From metastatic disease to no evidence of disease after conversion liver surgery in advanced gastric cancer with liver metastases: A case report.
abstract: Stage IV gastric cancer with liver metastases has a poor prognosis. Conversion surgery may enable long-term disease control in selected patients, but pathological complete response is rare and is usually defined only for surgically resected specimens. Here, a 54-year-old female with initially unresectable, HER2-negative, pMMR-by-IHC, EBER-positive gastric cancer and synchronous liver metastases received first-line XELOX plus tislelizumab for 4 cycles. Because of suspected oxaliplatin hypersensitivity, treatment was changed to cisplatin plus capecitabine plus tislelizumab for 3 cycles. After subsequent suspected platinum hypersensitivity, treatment was changed to capecitabine plus tislelizumab for 7 cycles. After 14 cycles, repeat endoscopic biopsy showed no tumor cells. Imaging showed significant regression of liver lesions. After multidisciplinary discussion, the patient underwent conversion liver surgery comprising resection of selected liver lesions and radiofrequency ablation of other liver lesions. R0 status was confirmed only for the resected liver specimens; ablated lesions had no pathological specimen. Histopathological examination of the resected liver specimens showed no residual viable tumor cells, consistent with pathological complete response in the resected liver lesions. The gastric primary was assessed as clinical complete response by endoscopy and biopsy. At last follow-up 1 month after surgery, imaging showed no evidence of disease; long-term outcome remains unknown. This case illustrates that selected patients with advanced gastric cancer and liver metastases may achieve a strong response to tislelizumab-based immunochemotherapy and liver-directed conversion treatment. However, the long-term benefit, the role of omitting gastrectomy, and the significance of FAPI/FDG discordance remain uncertain.

title: Differentiating disseminated cryptococcosis from pulmonary cryptococcosis: Roles of clinical characteristics and cryptococcal antigen.
abstract: Abstract Distinguishing disseminated cryptococcosis (DC) from localized pulmonary cryptococcosis (PC) is crucial due to divergent management and disparate prognoses. This study aimed to recognize associated factors for DC from PC in non-human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) patients. Accordingly, 475 pathologically confirmed cryptococcosis cases (391 PC and 84 DC) were retrospectively reviewed over a 20-year period at a tertiary hospital in China. Clinical, radiographic, dynamic serum cryptococcal antigen (CrAg) titer profiles, treatment and prognosis were analyzed. Patients with DC were significantly associated with a history of glucocorticoid therapy (16.7% vs. 5.6%; P = 0.001) and autoimmune diseases (16.7% vs. 6.1%; P = 0.001) compared with PC, aggressive thoracic computed tomography findings, including patchy exudation ( P = 0.001) and cavitation ( P = 0.009), and markedly higher baseline median serum CrAg titers (1:1280 vs. 1:80, P < 0.001). By multivariable analysis, CNS symptoms (adjusted OR [aOR] 131.12, 95% CI 10.21-1683.9, P = 0.001), chronic liver disease (aOR 15.21, 95% CI 1.06-217.69, P = 0.045), and baseline serum CrAg ≥1:80 (aOR 13.51, 95% CI 1.39-131.07, P = 0.025) remained independently associated with DC. An initial CrAg titer ≥ 1:80 should prompt careful CNS evaluation and consideration of lumbar puncture. Patients with DC had significantly longer median CrAg clearance ( P = 0.001) and antifungal duration (18 vs. 6 months), with higher mortality (9.5% vs. 1.0%; P < 0.001) compared to PC. Early risk-stratification is imperative to optimize interventions and improve survival.
