title: Regional blood-brain barrier dysfunction maps to lower performance in cognitive ageing.
abstract: Age-related cognitive decline is a common and growing public health challenge, associated with loss of independence, reduced quality of life, increased caregiver burden and substantial healthcare and societal costs. Yet cognitive decline in ageing is heterogeneous, and current clinical constructs do not reliably capture the underlying biological mechanisms or predict progression to dementia. This cross-sectional study examined whether blood-brain barrier dysfunction (BBBD) provides a biologically supported correlate of cognitive performance beyond clinical diagnosis. The study included 46 patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), 46 age-matched controls and 43 young controls. BBBD was assessed using dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI in 42 patients with MCI and all controls, alongside volumetric brain analysis. Standardized NeuroTrax cognitive assessment data were analysed for 41 MCI patients and 19 age-matched controls. BBBD was analysed using the BBBdetect software (Emagix Inc, Nova Scotia, Canada), quantifying voxelwise and region-wise blood-brain barrier permeability; volumetric analysis was performed using the Volbrain software; and cognitive performance was stratified into low- and high-performance subgroups based on modified z-scores. Compared with young controls, the older cohort (MCI patients combined with age-matched controls) showed significantly greater BBBD volume and regional extent. Permeability increased with age and showed marked inter-individual variability. Across participants, lower cognitive performance was associated with a greater number of regions exhibiting BBBD. Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified domain-specific spatial patterns of BBBD linked to poor performance in memory, executive, attention, verbal and motor domains, implicating frontal, cingulate, hippocampal, basal ganglia and cerebellar regions. In contrast, volumetric analyses revealed expected age-related reductions in grey and white matter and cortical thickness along with increased ventricular volume; however, these structural changes showed weak to no associations with cognitive performance. These findings suggest that BBBD is widespread in ageing and that regional BBBD maps to domain-specific cognitive deficits. BBBD thus emerges as a biologically relevant biomarker of age-related cognitive impairment and a potential therapeutic target for preserving cognitive function in ageing.

title: Metabolic connectivity and memory in mesial temporal lobe epilepsy.
abstract: Memory decline after anterior mesial temporal resection in mesial temporal lobe epilepsy with hippocampal sclerosis (MTLE-HS) remains incompletely explained by structural and clinical factors, suggesting that networks may contribute to cognitive vulnerability. We investigated whether presurgical metabolic connectivity (MC), derived from fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) and reflecting metabolic network organization, is associated with memory performance and postsurgical cognitive outcome in MTLE-HS. We studied 83 patients with MTLE-HS who underwent anterior mesial temporal resection. All had interictal FDG-PET and pre- and postsurgical neuropsychological testing. MC was computed using a normative connectivity framework and examined in relation to memory performance, analysed separately for left and right TLE. The effect of resection extent on cognitive outcome was also assessed. Presurgical analyses revealed distinct lateralized patterns. In right temporal lobe epilepsy (RTLE), immediate visual memory correlated positively with MC across widespread fronto-cingulate-temporal networks, frequently including the lesional hippocampus. In left temporal lobe epilepsy (LTLE), immediate verbal memory showed only negative correlations with extratemporal MC. In RTLE, presurgical MC also correlated with postsurgical change in immediate visual memory. Predominantly negative associations involved ipsilateral hippocampal-cingulate and fronto-temporal pathways, whereas positive correlations were confined to contralateral posterior cingulate connections with frontal and temporal regions. In LTLE, no significant correlations with postsurgical memory change were identified. Extent of resection did not correlate with cognitive outcome. MC was significantly associated with memory performance in MTLE-HS, showing clear lateralized differences. In RTLE, presurgical MC was associated with postsurgical outcome: ipsilateral hippocampal-cingulate connectivity was linked to decline, whereas contralateral posterior cingulate pathways supported preservation. No such associations were found in LTLE, consistent with more constrained network reorganization within left-lateralized verbal memory systems. title: Tegmental atrophy in isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder: ex vivo MRI-informed in vivo imaging.
abstract: Isolated rapid eye movement (REM) sleep behaviour disorder (iRBD) is an early-stage synucleinopathy characterized by brainstem pathology. In rodents, the pontine tegmentum contains a REM sleep centre, the sublaterodorsal nucleus, which expresses corticotropin-releasing hormone binding protein (CRHBP). While the involvement of brainstem pathophysiology is thus implicated in iRBD, its solid evidence remains scarce in humans due to the difficulty in identifying small brainstem nuclei with conventional MRI technology alone. Here, we aimed to detect tegmental atrophy in iRBD with voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analysis combined with a novel human brainstem atlas. Structural MRIs from 98 patients with iRBD and 114 controls were analysed to investigate grey matter volume using VBM. Our unique approach involved detailed assessments of the VBM results, guided by a high-resolution MRI-based atlas of the human brainstem. This brainstem atlas was founded on ex vivo MRI of 10 post-mortem human specimens. We validated it with CRHBP immunostaining, which aided in identifying putative REM sleep-regulating nuclei in humans. We applied this brainstem atlas to identify atrophy in specific brainstem regions in iRBD and correlate their volumes with clinical and polysomnographic measures. Voxel-based morphometry revealed a focal cluster of grey matter atrophy in the dorsal pontine tegmentum of iRBD patients, including the laterodorsal tegmental nucleus, ventral part (LDTgV) and the pedunculopontine tegmental nucleus (PTg). Our atlas-based analysis confirmed the LDTgV as the site of most conspicuous atrophy, revealing a significant volume reduction in iRBD patients compared with controls with a moderate effect size (Cohen's d = 0.44, Bonferroni-corrected P = 0.019). Furthermore, greater atrophy in the LDTgV and the PTg was associated with more severe autonomic dysfunction as measured by Scales for Outcomes in Parkinson's Disease-Autonomic dysfunction scores (partial r = -0.237, P = 0.021 and partial r = -0.236, P = 0.021, respectively). In 23 patients from whom quantitative polysomnographic data were available, LDTgV atrophy was correlated with the percentage ratio of REM sleep without atonia (partial r = -0.491, P = 0.028). Histological analysis confirmed that the LDTgV is selectively enriched with CRHBP-positive neurons, a putative marker for REM sleep-on neurons. We provided novel evidence for the involvement of LDTgV, the putative human homologue of the murine sublaterodorsal nucleus, in iRBD. The present findings advance our understanding of the neuroanatomical basis of iRBD and will contribute to the development of early biomarkers for α-synucleinopathies.

title: Cerebellar involvement in sporadic amyotrophic lateral sclerosis: a magnetic resonance spectroscopy study.
abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is increasingly recognized as a multisystem neurodegenerative disorder, and recent evidence suggests that the cerebellum may contribute to disease pathology, although cerebellar metabolic alterations have not previously been demonstrated in vivo. This study investigated cerebellar metabolic and structural changes using proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H-MRS) and volumetric imaging. Thirty patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (21 M, mean age 59.7 ± 7.6 years), 22 healthy controls (HC, 10 M, mean age 59.8 ± 9.6 years) and 16 individuals with hereditary spastic paraplegia type 4 (8 M, mean age 50.8 ± 12.5 years), a potential clinical mimic, underwent 3T MRI and 1H-MRS with a single-voxel positioned in the left cerebellar hemisphere. Patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis showed significant reductions in myo-inositol/creatinine (P = 0.01) and glutathione/creatinine (P = 0.005), compared with HC, together with selective volume loss in cerebellar lobules I-IV, V, VI, and Crus I. Among metabolites, glutathione/creatinine had the highest discriminative accuracy for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis versus both HC and spastic paraplegia type 4, with areas under the curve of 0.80 and 0.71, respectively. These findings reveal distinct cerebellar metabolic alterations in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, providing further evidence for cerebellar involvement in disease pathology and highlighting cerebellar 1H-MRS as a potential adjunct to diagnostic evaluation.

title: Clinical spectrum of penile intraepithelial neoplasia in a sexual health service: a retrospective case series.
abstract: Background Penile intraepithelial neoplasia (PeIN) is an uncommon precursor to invasive penile squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). Its heterogeneous appearance may overlap with inflammatory penile dermatoses, genital warts, or infection, potentially delaying diagnosis. We aimed to characterise the clinical spectrum, inflammatory context, biopsy triggers, histopathology, management, and outcomes of histopathologically confirmed PeIN presenting to a sexual health service. Methods We conducted a retrospective case series of patients with histopathologically confirmed low-grade or high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions, or invasive SCC, assessed at Melbourne Sexual Health Centre, Australia, from 2018-2025. Electronic records were reviewed for demographics, immune status, circumcision status, lesion site and morphology, symptoms, coexisting inflammatory disease, biopsy indications, histopathology, treatment, recurrence, and follow-up. Data were analysed descriptively. Results Thirteen patients aged 25-72 years were identified; four had lichen sclerosus and three had immunosuppression or immune-modifying therapy. Most were uncircumcised at diagnosis. Lesions predominantly involved the glans or inner foreskin, but also occurred on the shaft, and showed marked heterogeneity, including erythematous or white plaques, papules, warty or hyperkeratotic lesions, erosions, fissures, and ulcerated nodules. Symptoms ranged from none to pain, burning, itch, hypersensitivity, malodour, and non-healing sores. Several lesions initially appeared inflammatory or wart-like; sometimes in the setting of documented lichen sclerosus. Biopsy was generally prompted by persistence, focal hyperkeratosis or induration, ulceration or erosion, architectural change, progressive enlargement, or incomplete response to empiric therapy. Histopathology showed predominantly high-grade lesions; one patient had low-grade disease with biopsy-confirmed recurrence, and two had invasive SCC. All cases were HPV-associated by reported histopathological features and/or p16 positivity. Management was frequently multimodal and multidisciplinary, including circumcision, local or wide excision, partial penectomy, imiquimod, 5-fluorouracil, cryotherapy, and treatment of coexisting inflammation. Outcomes were generally favourable where documented, although recurrence or suspected recurrence occurred in some patients and ongoing surveillance was often required. Conclusions PeIN presenting to sexual health services is clinically diverse and commonly embedded within an inflammatory clinical narrative. Persistent or atypical penile lesions, particularly those showing focal change or incomplete treatment response, warrant a low threshold for biopsy and coordinated dermatology-urology management.

title: Real-time assessment of mitotic rate in malignant melanoma by ex vivo confocal microscopy.
abstract: Background Malignant melanoma has exhibited a significant increase in incidence over the past decade and remains the most common cause of skin cancer-related deaths. Early diagnosis and treatment are essential, as delays correlate with poorer clinical outcomes. Ex vivo confocal laser scanning microscopy (EVCM) enables intraoperative examination of fresh tissues within minutes and has shown potential for detecting morphological criteria and accurately determining Breslow thickness in melanoma. Objectives The aim of the present pilot study was to evaluate whether EVCM can also reliably assess the mitotic rate, an important prognostic marker influencing the indication for sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB). Methods 40 histologically confirmed melanomas from various anatomical sites were examined using the current gold standard of histopathology and EVCM. The confocal mitotic rate (CMR) and the histopathological mitotic rate (HMR) were statistically compared. In this context, two clinically relevant groups (0 mitoses/mm2 and ≥ 1 mitosis/mm2) were defined for analysis, taking into consideration the clinically significant thresholds typically used in histopathological assessment. Results Overall, 95.0% of melanomas were correctly assigned to the respective group. Malignant melanoma has exhibited a significant increase in incidence over the past decade and remains the most common cause of skin cancer-related deaths. Early diagnosis and treatment are essential, as delays correlate with poorer clinical outcomes. Ex vivo confocal laser scanning microscopy (EVCM) enables intraoperative examination of fresh tissues within minutes and has shown potential for detecting morphological criteria and accurately determining Breslow thickness in melanoma.

Objectives

The aim of the present pilot study was to evaluate whether EVCM can also reliably assess the mitotic rate, an important prognostic marker influencing the indication for sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB).

40 histologically confirmed melanomas from various anatomical sites were examined using the current gold standard of histopathology and EVCM. The confocal mitotic rate (CMR) and the histopathological mitotic rate (HMR) were statistically compared. In this context, two clinically relevant groups (0 mitoses/mm2 and ≥ 1 mitosis/mm2) were defined for analysis, taking into consideration the clinically significant thresholds typically used in histopathological assessment.

Results

Overall, 95.0% of melanomas were correctly assigned to the respective group. With a sensitivity of 100%, a specificity of 77.8%, a positive predictive value of 93.9% and a negative predictive value of 100%, EVCM demonstrated promising performance for detecting mitotic activity.

Conclusions

These findings emphasize the potential of EVCM for reliable detection of atypical mitotic figures. Prior to clinical implementation, prospective validation in larger, multicenter cohorts involving multiple EVCM experts is required.

title: Gratitude mediates the link of precuneus volume to depression in older women.
abstract: Depression in older people is a major contributor to global disease burden and functional impairment. While trait gratitude, a stable tendency to appreciate others' help, has been shown to alleviate depressive symptoms across populations, less is known about its neuroanatomical substrates and protective neuropsychological mechanisms against depression symptoms in aging populations. Here, we investigated the structural neural correlates of trait gratitude in 120 community-dwelling older women using voxel-based morphometry analysis of T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging data. First, the whole-brain correlation analysis identified a negative association between trait gratitude and regional gray matter volume (GMV) in the right precuneus. Mediation analyses further suggested that trait gratitude could mediate the impact of regional GMV in right precuneus on depression symptoms. Critically, supplemental analyses showed that the results persisted even after controlling for anxiety and stress symptoms, as well as general personality traits. Our study presents novel evidence for the neuroanatomical basis of trait gratitude in general older women and highlights a brain-personality-symptom pathway for protecting against depression in which GMV affects depressive symptoms via trait gratitude. These findings deepen understanding of gratitude's protective role in late-life mental health while highlighting potential neurostructural markers for resilience against depression.

title: Brain structure links extraversion to shyness in late adolescence.
abstract: Shyness is a prevalent psychological construct that can lead to psychopathology and negative developmental outcomes, yet its neurostructural substrates remain poorly understood, particularly during adolescence-a critical period for social and emotional development. This study examined the brain gray matter volume correlates of shyness and the potential mediating role of basic personality traits in 228 normal adolescents (aged 16-20 years). Participants underwent structural magnetic resonance imaging and completed the Cheek and Buss Shyness Scale and NEO Five-Factor Inventory. Whole-brain voxel-based morphometry and cross-validation prediction analyses revealed a positive association between shyness and gray matter volume in the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, a key region implicated in cognitive control and emotion regulation. Among the Big Five traits, only extraversion correlated with right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex gray matter volume and showed a significant indirect association with the gray matter volume-shyness link. Specifically, higher right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex gray matter volume was associated with lower extraversion, which in turn was associated with greater shyness; this indirect association was partial and remained significant after controlling for other personality traits. These results highlight the importance of integrating neural and personality factors in understanding shyness during this critical developmental period and offer potential targets for early identification and intervention.

title: Tongue Swab Mycobacterium tuberculosis Quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction for Community Screening of Asymptomatic Tuberculosis Versus Clinic-Based Triage of Symptomatic Tuberculosis.
abstract: Background Diagnostic performance of tongue swab Mycobacterium tuberculosis polymerase chain reaction (PCR) has been evaluated for triage of symptomatic tuberculosis (TB). It is unknown whether performance differs for detection of asymptomatic TB in community-based screening. Methods Tongue swabs were collected from adult household contacts of persons with TB (HHC cohort), and symptomatic adults presenting with presumptive TB (clinic cohort), at six South African sites. Drug-susceptible pulmonary TB was defined by positive sputum Xpert Ultra (excluding trace) or liquid culture, which were performed in all participants. Tongue swabs from participants with and without TB, matched by propensity score, were tested by high-volume quantitative PCR (qPCR) and, in the clinic cohort, also by sequence-specific magnetic capture (SSMaC) with qPCR. Results The clinic cohort included 217 participants with TB (100% symptomatic) and 437 participants without TB. The HHC cohort included 44 participants with TB (84.1% asymptomatic) and 136 participants without TB. In the clinic cohort, sensitivity of SSMaC with qPCR was 73.2% (specificity 94.6%), but not significantly higher than high-volume qPCR (63.8%; P = .14) (specificity 94.4%). Sensitivity of high-volume qPCR in the clinic cohort (63.8%) was significantly higher than the HHC cohort (34.1%; P = .0007) (specificity 91.9%). Among HHC, high-volume qPCR sensitivity was 35.1% for asymptomatic TB, 52.2% for TB with abnormal chest radiograph, and 100% for TB with high sputum Xpert Ultra grade. Conclusions Sensitivity of tongue swab high-volume qPCR in community-based, household screening for asymptomatic TB was low, approximately half that of facility-based triage for symptomatic TB, but increased with radiographic severity and sputum bacillary load.

title: Diffusion tensor MR neurography reveals altered sciatic and tibial nerve microstructure in chronic dialysis patients.
abstract: Introduction Uremic polyneuropathy is a complication of chronic kidney disease, presenting as a distal symmetric neuropathy mainly attributed to axonal damage. Electrophysiology provides limited insight into microstructural nerve alterations. Magnetic resonance neurography (MRN) may enable assessment of peripheral nerve integrity. This study aimed to quantify sciatic and tibial nerve microstructural changes in chronic dialysis patients and evaluate their clinical relevance. Methods Thirty patients on chronic dialysis (DP)-without prediabetes or diabetes-and 30 healthy controls (HCs) underwent MRN, including diffusion tensor imaging (DTI). All MRN datasets of the distal thigh (30/30) were suitable for analysis. Four lower-leg examinations in the patient cohort (26/30) and three in the healthy group (27/30) were excluded because of motion artifacts. Fractional anisotropy (FA) was defined as the primary imaging outcome, while axial diffusivity (AD) and radial diffusivity (RD) were analyzed as secondary metrics. Electrophysiological testing was not available in four patients in the dialysis cohort (26/30). Results were compared between groups and correlated with electrophysiological, clinical, and laboratory findings. Results FA of the sciatic (DP 0.44, HC 0.48, P < .001) and tibial nerve (DP 0.38, HC 0.43, P < .0001) and AD were significantly reduced in dialysis patients, while RD did not differ between groups. Lower FA correlated with electrophysiological measures, neuropathy scores, and was independently associated with group after adjustment for age, BMI, and sex. Subgroup analyses showed lower FA in patients fulfilling electrophysiological criteria for uremic polyneuropathy but no difference according to dialysis modality. Discussion The reduction in FA and AD, together with electrophysiological and clinical correlations, is compatible with a predominantly axonal pattern of peripheral nerve involvement in chronic dialysis patients. DTI detected peripheral nerve microstructural alterations associated with chronic dialysis. These findings support further longitudinal and disease control studies to determine the clinical utility of DTI as an imaging biomarker in chronic dialysis patients.

title: Association between Glycoprotein Acetylation-Indicated Inflammation and Small HDL Particle Number in Coronary Artery Disease.
abstract: Background Glycoprotein acetylation (GlycA) is a nuclear magnetic resonance-derived biomarker of systemic inflammation. GlycA shows statistical interaction with small HDL particle number (s-HDL-P) in relation to coronary artery disease (CAD). This study examines the confounding effects of GlycA-related glycoproteins, hypertriglyceridemia, and s-HDL-P on CAD risk. Methods Plasma samples from 752 participants in the CATHGEN biorepository were size-fractionated by asymmetric flow field-flow fractionation and analyzed by targeted proteomics and lipidomics. Fraction concentrations were converted to HDL particle number using a volumetric approach based on apolipoprotein A-I (APOA1) concentration, HDL size, and lipoprotein lipid composition. Correlations between GlycA, glycoproteins, total triglyceride (TG), HDL composition and HDL particle number, and their associations with CAD were assessed using multivariate least-squares fit and nominal logistic regression analysis, respectively. Results Acute-phase inflammation-related glycoproteins (GlycA-proteins) correlated strongly with GlycA. However, the size-distribution profiles of GlycA-proteins were consistent with circulation as free dimers/trimers, and their lack of overlap with APOA1 profiles suggested no detectable HDL binding. In contrast, apolipoproteins and lipid transfer proteins showed size-profile shifts relative to APOA1 consistent with HDL binding. s-HDL-P showed an inverse association with GlycA, most significantly at low TG levels. In CAD models, significant GlycA × s-HDL-P interaction emerged only when TG was included as a covariate. CAD correlated with lipoprotein lipids, apolipoproteins, and lipid transfer proteins that influence lipoprotein remodeling. Conclusions GlycA-proteins circulate freely without direct HDL binding. The empirical GlycA × s-HDL-P interaction is consistent with indirect coupling between systemic inflammation and altered lipoprotein remodeling associated with CAD risk.

In CAD models, significant GlycA × s-HDL-P interaction emerged only when TG was included as a covariate. CAD correlated with lipoprotein lipids, apolipoproteins, and lipid transfer proteins that influence lipoprotein remodeling.

Conclusions

GlycA-proteins circulate freely without direct HDL binding. The empirical GlycA × s-HDL-P interaction is consistent with indirect coupling between systemic inflammation and altered lipoprotein remodeling associated with CAD risk.

title: Improved plaque composition from intensive medical treatment in women with angina and non-obstructive coronary disease.
abstract: Aims Among women with suspected ischaemia and non-obstructive coronary artery disease (INOCA), the temporal effect of combination intensive medical treatment (IMT) with angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors or receptor blockers, statins, and aspirin on coronary plaque composition is not known. This prospective ancillary study examined changes in atherosclerotic plaque volumes and composition (percentage of total plaque volume) over time between IMT and usual care (UC). Methods and results Participants from the randomized WARRIOR trial with the presence of plaque on their first coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) were enrolled for a follow-up CCTA at least 2 years after randomization. Volumes and volumetric composition (percentage of total plaque volume) of non-calcified plaque (NCP), low-density NCP (LD-NCP, defined as NCP <30 HU), and calcified plaque (CP) were quantified over the coronary tree in the serial scans.Participants (n = 186) completed both scans with good image quality (94 IMT arm and 92 UC arm). Overall mean age was 61.0 years (SD ±10.9), and there were no statistically significant differences in baseline risk factors, plaque volumes, or statin treatment between the arms.There was a greater bi-annualized increase in CP volume [ΔCP volume (mm3)] in the IMT arm, 6.2 (SD ±15.5) compared to the UC arm, 3.9 (SD ±16.0), P = 0.013, and a consistent greater reduction in NCP composition [ΔNCP composition (%)] in the IMT arm, -3.9 (SD ±7.7) compared to the UC arm, -1.5 (SD ±5.8), P = 0.003, with no increase in total plaque volume. Conclusion In women with suspected INOCA, IMT reduces NCP volumetric composition to a greater extent than UC and may promote plaque stabilization.

title: Complex relationship between iron status and outcomes of STEMI: hypothesis-generating study.
abstract: Aims Iron deficiency (ID) is common amongst patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Its impact on outcomes remains contested. Previous studies reported favourable or adverse impacts depending on outcome measures, sampling timepoints, ID definition and follow-up duration. This study systematically characterises the prognostic impact of iron status on short-term, mid-term and long-term outcomes, and evaluates the effect of sampling timepoint and ID definition on these prognostic relationships. Methods & results We performed an observational cohort study in patients with acute STEMI (n = 167) and no prior heart failure (HF). Iron markers were sampled at presentation, and successive timepoints thereafter. Cardiac Magnetic Resonance was performed at 2 days and 6 months. Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), consisting of new-onset HF, recurrent MI or cardiac death were recorded over 4.5 years. Mechanisms were evaluated in a preclinical model of MI.ID was common at presentation, affecting between 44.9% and 67%, depending on ID definition. Tsat <20%, serum iron<13μM, or European Society of Cardiology's definition, but not ferritin<100μg/L, independently predicted lower risk of MACE. Lower Tsat at presentation predicted attenuated infarct and non-infarct T1, and smaller left ventricular volumes at 2 days. This prognostic effect was weakened by delayed sampling. Lower Tsat and serum iron in the post-acute timepoints, but not at presentation, predicted lower myocardial salvage at 6 months. In mice, MI triggered an acute myocardial labile iron storm and early LV remodelling, progressing to HF. Baseline ID and acute iron chelation averted these effects. Conclusions This study gives rise to the hypothesis that ID at presentation with STEMI improves long-term outcomes by attenuating myocardial injury. It reconciles previous conflicting reports by revealing the confounding effects of delayed sampling, and non-interchangeability of different ID definitions. It suggests iron chelation in the acute stage, followed by post-acute iron repletion might improve long-term outcomes.

title: Lamina dura thickening in patients on antiresorptive therapy as a radiographic risk indicator of medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw: a retrospective longitudinal cohort study.
abstract: Aims This study investigated whether antiresorptive drug (ARD) therapy is associated with lamina dura (LD) thickening, defined as a radiographic increase in the thickness of the normally thin, radiopaque cortical line surrounding the tooth root. It further evaluated whether LD thickening serves as a radiographic marker and risk indicator for medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ). Methods Panoramic radiographs from 65 ARD-treated patients (University Hospital Leuven) and 65 age- and sex-matched controls were analyzed. Inclusion criteria were prior oncological diagnosis, high-dose intravenous ARD, and radiographs before and after therapy. Three blinded oral and maxillofacial radiologists categorized LD appearance into 4 grades: (0) not/barely visible, (1) normal, (2) mild thickening, and (3) marked thickening. Group differences and longitudinal changes were evaluated using appropriate non-parametric and time-to-event analyses. Results Among 130 participants, LD thickness remained stable in controls but increased in ARD-treated patients (P < .001). Within the ARD group, LD thickening changed over time (P < .001): 30.6% showed no change, 55.4% developed mild thickening, and 13.8% marked thickening. Controls showed minimal change (P = .011), with 9.2% developing mild thickening. Kaplan-Meier analysis estimated a median time to LD thickening of 27 months, with a higher thickening probability in ARD-treated patients than controls (P < .001). Lamina dura thickening was not directly associated with MRONJ (P = .39). Conclusion Lamina dura thickening is strongly associated with long-term ARD exposure and shows progressive changes. Although not directly associated with MRONJ in this cohort, it may still represent a potential risk indicator, warranting confirmation in further studies.

title: Diagnostic performance of a novel wireless direct-conversion intraoral sensor versus complementary metal-oxide semiconductor and photostimulable storage phosphor systems for proximal caries detection: an ex vivo study.
abstract: Objectives To compare the diagnostic accuracy of a new wireless direct-conversion digital intraoral sensor to current indirect-conversion complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS) and photostimulable storage phosphor (PSP) sensors for detecting proximal caries. Methods The sample in this ex vivo study were 28 human premolars with 21 micro-CT verified non-cavitated proximal dental carious lesions. Images were obtained using 3 digital intraoral systems: a wireless direct-conversion sensor, a wired indirect-conversion CMOS sensor, and a PSP sensor. A custom phantom was constructed providing a limited dental arch segment comprising a molar, first premolar, and canine. The premolar was substituted and the phantom imaged using each intraoral system with (filtered) and without (raw) the application of a manufacturer-recommended enhancements, providing 168 images. Eight oral radiologists assessed the images using a 5-point scale. Receiver operating characteristic analysis was performed to calculate sensitivity, specificity, and the area under the curve (AUC) and compared across modalities using 2-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) with post hoc Tukey's test at an a priori level of significance of 0.05. Results The AUC ranged from 0.58 to 0.73 (sensitivity range: 0.21-0.68, specificity range: 0.69-0.92). The wireless direct-conversion sensor (0.72 ± 0.06) showed diagnostic performance comparable to CMOS (0.72 ± 0.06) and superior to PSP (0.58 ± 0.07) for raw images (P < .001). The direct-conversion sensor without image enhancement (0.68 ± 0.18) demonstrated the highest sensitivity, whereas the PSP without image enhancement (0.21 ± 0.09) had the lowest sensitivity. Application of image enhancement improved PSP performance (0.48 ± 0.16), approximating that of the other systems. Conclusions Based on this ex vivo study, the wireless direct-conversion and CMOS sensors demonstrated similar diagnostic performance, superior to PSP in unfiltered conditions. These findings should be interpreted in light of the ex vivo design and modest sample size.

title: Artificial intelligence for reducing metal artifacts in dental CBCT images: a systematic review.
abstract: Objectives The presence of metallic restorations introduces severe artifacts that compromise the diagnostic accuracy of cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) images. This systematic review aims to evaluate the effectiveness of artificial intelligence (AI) techniques in reducing metal artifacts in dental CBCT images. Methods A comprehensive literature search was conducted across 6 databases up until April 2025, using keywords related to AI and CBCT artifact reduction. Studies were selected based on the eligibility criteria, focusing on AI models trained on human CBCT scans targeting dental regions. Data extraction and risk of bias assessment (using the QUADAS-2 tool) were performed independently by several reviewers accordingly. Results Ten studies published between 2019 and 2025 met the eligibility criteria. The majority of included studies had a high risk of bias. The most employed deep learning architectures were U-Net, GANs, and transformer-based models. Quantitative metrics like SSIM, PSNR, and RMSE demonstrated consistent improvements in image quality, while qualitative assessments confirmed superior artifact suppression and anatomical detail preservation compared to conventional methods. Transformer-based and physics-informed dual-domain networks performed superior to traditional image-only U-Nets in both quantitative fidelity and visual artifact suppression. Conclusions AI-based approaches show promising potential in enhancing CBCT image fidelity by effectively mitigating metal-induced distortions. Despite encouraging results, the broader clinical adoption of such techniques requires standardized evaluation protocols, training models using open-access datasets, and further trials to validate diagnostic impact and generalizability.

title: Automatic detection of panoramic positioning errors and development of an objective image quality scoring system using deep learning.
abstract: Objectives To develop a deep learning model capable of automatically detecting common positioning errors in panoramic radiographs and to establish an error-based objective 10-point image quality scoring system aligned with expert evaluation. Methods A total of 4390 panoramic radiographs were retrospectively annotated for 7 clinically relevant positioning errors (including chin position, head rotation/tilt, bite position, tongue position, cervical spine positioning, and anatomical coverage) associated with diagnostically meaningful geometric distortion or anatomical superimposition by 2 experienced oral radiologists. A multi-label deep learning model based on a modified residual network was trained to detect all errors simultaneously. An independent dataset of 510 radiographs was scored for subjective image quality on a 10-point scale. Multiple linear regression was used to estimate the independent contribution of each positioning error to subjective image quality and to derive an objective scoring system established by converting regression-derived weights of significant errors into standardized point deductions. Results High annotation and scoring reliability were achieved (Kappa: 0.879-0.953; ICC: 0.838). The model achieved high performance across all error types, with accuracy ranging from 88.40% to 96.00% and area under the curve values between 98.17 and 99.37. Several positioning errors were associated with lower subjective image quality scores (P < .001). The resulting error-weighted objective score showed moderate correlation with expert ratings (r = 0.673, P < .001). Conclusions The proposed system enables accurate detection of positioning errors and provides a structured and interpretable, error-based surrogate measure of perceived panoramic image quality. Advances in knowledge This study presents an error-specific, data-driven framework for objective assessment of panoramic image acquisition quality, enhancing the interpretability and standardization of image quality evaluation.

title: SinusNet+: deep condition-label-free segmentation of maxillary sinus conditions in cone-beam CT images.
abstract: Objectives Segmentation of maxillary sinus conditions (MSC) in cone-beam CT (CBCT) images may support preoperative assessment in the posterior maxilla, including implant planning and sinus floor augmentation. Supervised deep learning methods for MSC segmentation typically rely on labor-intensive manual annotation of MSC for network training. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a condition-label-free deep learning framework (SinusNet+) for MSC segmentation in CBCT images, in which network training does not require manual MSC annotations and instead relies on synthetic conditions generated within the normal maxillary sinus (MS). Methods To generate synthetic MSC in normal MS, a synthetic condition generator was introduced to simulate MSC within the normal MS by varying texture, shape, and noise, thereby approximating a range of radiographic appearances of MSC in CBCT images. Results SinusNet+ achieved an average Dice similarity coefficient of 0.820 ± 0.110, precision of 0.878±0.061, and recall of 0.777±0.145, respectively. The proposed method outperformed unsupervised baselines and achieved segmentation performance comparable to that of the supervised approach. Conclusions The proposed framework demonstrates the feasibility of condition-label-free segmentation of MSC in CBCT images, while still requiring anatomical annotation of the normal MS during dataset preparation.

title: Novel marker-based cone-beam CT registration for enhanced accuracy in dental implant planning.
abstract: Objectives Accurate image registration is essential for successful digital dental implant planning. Surface-based registration, commonly used in clinical software, is sensitive to cone-beam CT (CBCT) artifacts and relies on manual landmark selection, potentially reducing accuracy. Marker-based registration offers improved precision but is underused due to its technical complexity and time demands. The purpose of this ex-vivo study was to evaluate the accuracy of a novel marker-based registration method using limited-view CBCT reconstructions derived from 2 orthogonal projection images and to compare it with a conventional surface-based registration method. Methods An ex-vivo model consisting of a maxillary arch with removable 3D-printed teeth and a radiographic guide containing radiographic markers was used to simulate 5 metal artifact conditions. Full-view CBCT scans were acquired for each condition. For the conventional method, 3 examiners independently performed dual-scan registrations using user-defined surface landmarks on full CBCT reconstructions. For the proposed method, examiners selected orthogonal projection images where markers were clearly visible and limited-view reconstructions were generated to identify marker centroids. Registration error was measured as the point-to-point distance between corresponding surface reference points, standardized to a common frame of reference. Inter-rater reliability was also assessed. Results Both methods maintained consistent performance across all artifact conditions. The proposed method demonstrated greater accuracy, with lower point-to-point registration errors and less spatial variation. Inter-rater reliability was excellent for the proposed method and good for the conventional approach. Conclusion The proposed marker-based registration method using orthogonal projection images and limited-view CBCT reconstructions showed higher accuracy than conventional surface-based registration under controlled ex-vivo conditions. Although the workflow currently requires additional examiner input, it may improve precision in dual-scan protocols for implant planning. Future clinical studies and software developments are required to support clinical implementation.

title: Does the radiographic image format influence the detection of fractured endodontic instruments in gutta-percha-filled canals?
abstract: Objective To evaluate the influence of different image file formats on the accuracy of detecting fractured endodontic instruments in gutta-percha-filled root canals. Methods Thirty-two mandibular molars were instrumented and divided into 2 groups: case (n = 15), which received a 2 mm fragment of a #35 K-file inside the mesial canal, and control (n = 17), without the fragment. Subsequently, all canals received gutta-percha, and each tooth was placed into a dry human mandible for acquiring radiographs. The radiographs were exported in TIFF, JPEG, BMP, PNG, and DICOM formats, resulting in 160 images (32 radiographs × 5 formats). Six radiologists evaluated the radiographs using a 5-point scale to determine the presence or absence of the fractured instrument. Area under the ROC curve, sensitivity, and specificity were calculated for each evaluator, along with a one-way ANOVA to compare the formats, adopting a 5% significance level. Results The image file format did not significantly influence the accuracy (P = .767), sensitivity (P = .307), or specificity (P = .999) in detecting fractured endodontic instruments in filled canals. Conclusions The study showed similar performance across the image file formats tested for detecting fractured instruments. These results suggest that commonly used and compatible formats can be used without compromising diagnostic accuracy. Advances in knowledge Instrument fracture is one of the most challenging complications in endodontic treatments, and digital periapical radiographs are widely used in diagnosing this occurrence. The detection and localization of the fragment inside the canal are essential for a favorable prognosis.

title: From CBCT to Synthesized Extraoral Bitewing: A Patient-Specific Pipeline for Dose- and Cost-Free 2D Information Presentation and Clinical Decision Support.
abstract: To evaluate whether synthesized extraoral bitewing views generated from existing CBCT scans can support posterior-tooth assessment when CBCT is the initial imaging modality, without additional radiographic acquisition. We retrospectively assembled 60 CBCT scans from three datasets encompassing diverse posterior jaw morphologies. We developed a computational pipeline to compute a patient specific dental arch, define a focal trough, and simulate extraoral bitewing acquisition using a panoramic inspired rotating source trajectory. Synthetic projections were generated using a Beer-Lambert forward model implemented in TIGRE and reconstructed into right and left synthesized extraoral bitewing views. Eight observers, including dental students and residents in endodontics, periodontics, and oral radiology scored posterior teeth for caries, periapical lesions, and periodontal bone loss using original CBCT images and synthesized extraoral bitewing views in separate sessions. A consensus of two oral radiology experts served as the reference. Performance was evaluated with false positive and false negative rates, specificity, F1 score, and AUC. Inter observer agreement was assessed with (weighted) kappa. Differences in AUC (ΔAUC) between CBCT and synthesized extraoral bitewing views were evaluated using bootstrap-derived 95% confidence intervals. Compared with CBCT alone, synthesized extraoral bitewing views were associated with lower overdiagnosis for dental caries and periapical lesions (95% CI, 5.87-12.00 and 3.87-8.12,respectively) and reduced underdiagnosis for periodontal bone loss (95% CI, 10.12-18.37). Synthesized extraoral bitewing views showed higher ordinal AUC for dental caries and periodontal bone loss (mean ΔAUC,-0.12 to - 0.05 and -0.11 to - 0.04,respectively). No consistent improvement was observed for periapical lesion AUC, possibly due to small sample size and limited power. When CBCT is the initial imaging modality, synthesized extraoral bitewing views derived from the existing scan may provide a complementary two-dimensional visualization for posterior-tooth assessment. In this reader study, the derived views were associated with shorter interpretation time and task-dependent changes in diagnostic performance.

abstract: To develop and internally validate cone-beam computed tomography radiomics for recorded clinicoradiologic classification of osteosclerosis, cemento-osseous dysplasia and odontoma, with secondary same-case three-dimensional convolutional neural-network benchmarking. This retrospective single-centre study included 126 lesions from 126 patients. From manual three-dimensional segmentations, 107 original radiomics features were extracted. A class-weighted least absolute shrinkage and selection operator one-vs-rest logistic-regression model was evaluated using 100 repeats of stratified five-fold held-out resampling. No independent histopathology report was retrievable in the retained study archive. A secondary strict 124-lesion three-dimensional analysis used 0.30-mm isotropic variable-size lesion-centred inputs, at least 5 mm of physical context and nested architecture/epoch selection; locked radiomics was evaluated on the same cases and outer folds. Primary radiomics achieved accuracy 0.825, balanced accuracy 0.842, macro F1-score 0.834 and macro area under the curve 0.932. In the matched 124-lesion analysis, macro area under the curve was 0.935 (95% bias-corrected and accelerated confidence interval 0.889-0.963) for radiomics and 0.601 (0.516-0.682) for the nested three-dimensional network. The network showed marked odontoma-class collapse (sensitivity 1/22, 0.045). Radiomics showed promising internal discrimination of the recorded labels, whereas the secondary three-dimensional benchmark was unstable for odontoma in this small cohort. These findings do not establish diagnostic accuracy against histopathology or general algorithmic superiority; external validation, standardised imaging and stronger reference standards are required. This study extends cone-beam computed tomography radiomics to radiopaque/mineralised jaw-lesion recorded labels and reports a same-case nested three-dimensional benchmark with explicit disclosure of class-specific failure.

title: Contemporary multicentre validation and comparative performance of Day 1 prognostic scores in acute severe ulcerative colitis.
abstract: Background and aims Early identification of steroid non-response in acute severe ulcerative colitis (ASUC) is critical to guide timely escalation of therapy. Several Day 1 prognostic scores have been proposed, but their comparative performance in contemporary cohorts remains uncertain, with limited direct head-to-head validation in real-world populations. We aimed to validate and directly compare the performance of previously proposed Day 1 prognostic scores, including the Admission Model for Intensification of Therapy in Acute Severe Colitis (ADMIT-ASC), the Albumin-C reactive protein-Endoscopy (ACE) index, and the Risk of Rescue (ROR) score, in a contemporary multicenter ASUC cohort. Methods We conducted a multicenter retrospective study of adults hospitalized with ASUC across three tertiary Australian centers between 2018 and 2023. The performance of ADMIT-ASC, ACE, and ROR scores for predicting steroid non-response, as defined by the Oxford criteria, was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Results Among 238 patients, 134 (56.3%) met criteria for steroid non-response and required medical rescue therapy. All three scores demonstrated moderate discrimination, with AUROC highest for ROR (0.72), followed by ADMIT-ASC (0.68) and ACE (0.66) (P = .17). At published thresholds, ADMIT-ASC and ACE demonstrated high specificity but low sensitivity, whereas ROR provided greater sensitivity with lower specificity. In subgroup analyses, the discriminative performance of the Day 1 scores was broadly similar in biologic-naive and biologic-exposed patients. Conclusion Day 1 prognostic scores demonstrate moderate performance in contemporary ASUC, with differing trade-offs between sensitivity and specificity. These findings support the use of Day 1 risk scores as adjuncts to early clinical decision-making in ASUC.

title: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance derived myocardial strain: applications, acquisition techniques, analysis, and reporting.
abstract: Myocardial strain imaging enables quantification of cardiac deformation. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) is well suited for strain assessment due to the ability to image in any given plane with high spatial and contrast resolution. CMR strain measures have incremental diagnostic and prognostic utility over conventional clinical imaging parameters across disease states. Routine integration of CMR strain assessment in clinical practice has been hindered by the lack of agreement on imaging protocols and analysis methods, variability due to noise sensitivity, and a paucity of robust normative age-, sex- and ethnicity-specific reference ranges. In recognition of the expanding applications of strain techniques in clinical and research CMR, this joint SCMR/RSNA/EACVI scientific statement integrates data from original research studies, guidelines, and opinions from experts across the field to guide responsible and evidence-based utilization of CMR strain.

title: Impact of the Extent, Pattern, and Location of Replacement Myocardial Fibrosis on Clinical Outcomes in Aortic Regurgitation.
abstract: Aims The prognostic significance of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE)-detected replacement myocardial fibrosis in aortic regurgitation (AR) remains incompletely understood. This study aims to explore the association between the extent, pattern, and location of LGE and clinical outcomes in patients with chronic AR. Methods and results Between 2010 and 2024, consecutive patients with moderate-to-severe AR and no significant coronary artery stenosis who underwent contrast-enhanced cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) were included. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as cardiovascular mortality, heart transplantation, or rehospitalization for heart failure. The association between LGE characteristics and MACE was evaluated. Overall, 363 patients (mean age 52.6 ± 14.2 years; 54 female) were included. Over a median follow-up of 56.6 months, 73 patients experienced MACE. LGE was present in 200 patients (55.1%). An LGE extent threshold of 2.6% provided robust risk stratification, yielding the highest C-index of 0.797, a likelihood ratio chi-square of 97.30, and the lowest Akaike information criterion of 681.06. Furthermore, predominant subendocardial-involved LGE was present in 13.5% of LGE-positive patients and was independently associated with MACE after adjusting for LGE extent (HR 3.028; 95% CI 1.216-7.539; P = 0.017). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated that patients with both LGE extent >2.6% and predominant subendocardial-involved LGE pattern were at the highest risk of MACE. Conclusions In AR, an LGE extent > 2.6% predicts MACE better than LGE presence alone. Furthermore, non-ischemic predominant subendocardial-involved LGE is independently associated with MACE. The coexistence of both features further amplifies the risk of MACE.

title: Giant cardiac hemangioma: case report and literature review.
abstract: Introduction Primary cardiac tumours are rare, with haemangiomas constituting only 2% of benign cardiac tumours. Although benign, these lesions can compress adjacent cardiac structures, leading to symptoms such as arrhythmias, heart failure, or even sudden death. This study presents a rare case of a giant cardiac haemangioma and provides a review of the current literature on its diagnosis and management. Case report A 58-year-old female presented with progressive abdominal pain and dyspnoea. Imaging revealed a large, heterogeneous mass in the pericardial sac measuring 11.9 × 11.7 × 6.7 cm. Complete surgical resection was performed without complications. Histopathological analysis confirmed the diagnosis of a cavernous haemangioma. Postoperative recovery was uneventful, and follow-up imaging showed no residual mass or functional impairment. Discussion Cardiac haemangiomas are rare and pose significant diagnostic challenges. Advanced imaging modalities, such as magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography (CT), are essential for accurate diagnosis and surgical planning. Complete tumour resection remains the treatment of choice, ensuring a favourable prognosis and minimal risk of recurrence. Conclusion Effective management of giant cardiac haemangiomas requires early diagnosis, precise imaging, and complete surgical resection. Long-term follow-up is necessary to monitor for recurrence and ensure optimal outcomes.
originalAbstract:
Introduction

Primary cardiac tumours are rare, with haemangiomas constituting only 2% of benign cardiac tumours. Although benign, these lesions can compress adjacent cardiac structures, leading to symptoms such as arrhythmias, heart failure, or even sudden death. This study presents a rare case of a giant cardiac haemangioma and provides a review of the current literature on its diagnosis and management.

Case report

A 58-year-old female presented with progressive abdominal pain and dyspnoea. Imaging revealed a large, heterogeneous mass in the pericardial sac measuring 11.9 × 11.7 × 6.7 cm. Complete surgical resection was performed without complications. Histopathological analysis confirmed the diagnosis of a cavernous haemangioma. Postoperative recovery was uneventful, and follow-up imaging showed no residual mass or functional impairment.

Discussion

Cardiac haemangiomas are rare and pose significant diagnostic challenges. Advanced imaging modalities, such as magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography (CT), are essential for accurate diagnosis and surgical planning. Complete tumour resection remains the treatment of choice, ensuring a favourable prognosis and minimal risk of recurrence.

Conclusion

Effective management of giant cardiac haemangiomas requires early diagnosis, precise imaging, and complete surgical resection. Long-term follow-up is necessary to monitor for recurrence and ensure optimal outcomes.

title: Coral reef aorta demonstrated by serial computed tomography: a case report.
abstract: Coral reef aorta (CRA) is a rare vascular disorder characterized by dense, protruding calcified plaques within the abdominal aorta, often resulting in ischaemic symptoms. Because of its rarity and atypical presentation, CRA is frequently diagnosed at an advanced stage. A 50-year-old male smoker with hypertension and hyperlipidaemia presented with progressive lower extremity symptoms. Four years before presentation, he developed bilateral lower limb numbness and was diagnosed with lumbar disc herniation, which likely masked the underlying vascular disease. One year before presentation, he developed intermittent claudication after ∼10 min of walking, followed by severe bilateral rest pain 1 month before presentation. The ankle-brachial index (ABI) was markedly reduced to 0.49 bilaterally. Computed tomography (CT) revealed extensive calcified plaques causing near occlusion of the infrarenal abdominal aorta. Serial CT over 6 years demonstrated progressive intraluminal calcification, facilitating diagnosis and treatment planning. title: When to stop monitoring pituitary stalk thickening?
abstract: Pituitary stalk thickening (PST) in adults may arise from neoplastic, inflammatory, infectious, or congenital disease, yet the underlying cause frequently remains undetermined after initial evaluation. For patients without an established diagnosis, no adult-specific data defines how long magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) surveillance should be maintained. Current expert reviews recommend early reassessment at 3-6 months, followed by longitudinal imaging for approximately 3-5 years. Among initially indeterminate lesions, spontaneous regression is more likely than the progression, although late diagnosis of histiocytic disease can nevertheless occur. We suggest reducing MRI frequency after sustained stability and considering discontinuation only in carefully selected low-risk adults, while maintaining longer surveillance whenever endocrine, radiological, or systemic risk features persist.

title: Predominantly mild thrombocytopenia, haematoma expansion and clinical outcomes in intracerebral haemorrhage.
abstract: Introduction Evidence regarding the prognostic significance of thrombocytopenia in spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage (ICH) remains limited and inconsistent. We investigated its associations with haematoma expansion (HE), functional outcomes and mortality. Patients and methods We retrospectively analysed prospectively collected data from consecutive patients with spontaneous ICH in a single-centre registry between August 2022 and March 2025. Thrombocytopenia was defined as an admission platelet count <150 × 109/L. HE was defined as a haematoma-volume increase >6 mL or >33% on follow-up noncontrast computed tomography. Poor functional outcome was defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 3-6 at 3 months. Associations were assessed using multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic splines, ordinal regression and sensitivity analyses. Results Among 496 patients, 106 (21.4%) had thrombocytopenia; 368 were included in the HE analysis. After adjustment, thrombocytopenia showed no statistically significant association with HE (adjusted OR 0.97, 95% CI, 0.52-1.76; P = .920), 3-month poor functional outcome (adjusted OR 0.88, 95% CI, 0.46-1.66; P = .693), or 3-month mortality (adjusted OR 1.43, 95% CI, 0.70-2.89; P = .324). Restricted cubic spline analysis showed no statistically significant overall association and the test for nonlinearity was not statistically significant. Findings were similar across platelet-count categories, continuous haematoma-volume changes, ordinal mRS analyses and sensitivity analyses addressing imaging timing, early surgery, acute treatments and prior anticoagulant use. Discussion Admission thrombocytopenia showed no statistically significant association with HE, poor functional outcome, or mortality after ICH. Because few patients had platelet counts <100 × 109/L, these findings mainly apply to mild thrombocytopenia.

title: Genetic analysis of bone morphometry and ivory vertebrae in threespine stickleback.
abstract: Previous genetic studies of skeletal variation in threespine stickleback fish (Gasterosteus aculeatus) have focused primarily on striking morphological differences. Here, we examine the largely unexplored genetic architecture of internal bone microstructural variation between marine and freshwater stickleback. Micro-computed tomography X-ray analysis revealed differences in the porosity, bone thickness, and bone volume fraction within armor plates and vertebrae from a marine and freshwater stickleback. Quantitative trait locus mapping in F2 progeny from a marine × freshwater stickleback cross identified a significant locus on chromosome 4 influencing multiple aspects of armor plate internal microstructure. This locus overlaps the well-characterized Eda region previously known to control armor plate number and size. Co-mapping of bone microstructure could be due to pleiotropic effects of Eda on multiple aspects of plate development or to changes in closely linked genes including Itm2a, which also plays a role in bone formation. Most bone microstructure traits in vertebrae showed weak or no genetic signal, consistent with a polygenic architecture. However, we identified a highly significant locus on chromosome 17 that is strongly associated with abnormally thickened "ivory vertebrae" that occurred in 8.4% of F2 offspring. This phenotype resembles Paget's disease in humans, and the major locus region contains Tnfrsf1b, the stickleback ortholog of a human Paget's disease susceptibility gene TNFRSF11A. Together, our findings identify genetic loci underlying natural variation in bone microstructure in wild fish and reveal a candidate gene associated with a disease-like skeletal phenotype, highlighting stickleback as a model for studying both evolutionary and pathological bone biology.

title: Structured reporting of diagnostic hysteroscopy findings in women with reproductive disorders: an ESGE-ESHRE-IFFS international consensus†ǂ.
abstract: Study question How should the findings of diagnostic hysteroscopy in women with reproductive disorders be reported? Summary answer This collaborative document by the European Society for Gynaecological Endoscopy (ESGE), the ESHRE, and the International Federation of Fertility Societies (IFFS) provides the first detailed structured reporting template for diagnostic hysteroscopy findings in women with reproductive disorders. What is known already Despite its widespread use in women with reproductive disorders, no standardized framework currently exists for reporting of hysteroscopic findings. This lack of uniformity may limit the utility of the procedure and contribute to substantial heterogeneity among operators and centers. As a result, the reproducibility of hysteroscopy is limited, making it difficult to conduct robust studies that define its prognostic value in specific patient subgroups. Study design, size, duration A dedicated working group from ESGE, ESHRE, and IFFS collaborated to develop a consensus for comprehensive structured reporting of diagnostic hysteroscopy findings in women with reproductive problems. Participants/materials, setting, methods This consensus paper focuses on grouping diagnostic hysteroscopic findings, structuring their reporting, and adopting standardized terminology for women with reproductive disorders. The virtual Nominal Group Technique, a structured consensus-building method, was adopted to ensure equal contribution from all members in the development of the final consensus. Main results and the role of chance The document provides a structured reporting of hysteroscopic findings into five sections, each systematically capturing patient characteristics, procedural findings, and pathological observations as follows: patient's characteristics, and findings from the vagina, cervix, uterine cavity, endometrium, and tubal ostia. Limitations, reasons for caution The inclusion of a finding in this structured report is not a proof of its clinical significance, but it could be used as a validation tool for further research. Wider implications of the findings The standardized reporting of hysteroscopic findings promotes consistent data collection across centers and could help inform research and exchange of clinical experience, enhancing the value of hysteroscopy in fertility evaluation. Funding No external funding was received for the development of the consensus process or manuscript preparation. Disclosures All authors declare that they have no competing interests. Trial registration number N/A.

Despite its widespread use in women with reproductive disorders, no standardized framework currently exists for reporting of hysteroscopic findings. This lack of uniformity may limit the utility of the procedure and contribute to substantial heterogeneity among operators and centers. As a result, the reproducibility of hysteroscopy is limited, making it difficult to conduct robust studies that define its prognostic value in specific patient subgroups.

A dedicated working group from ESGE, ESHRE, and IFFS collaborated to develop a consensus for comprehensive structured reporting of diagnostic hysteroscopy findings in women with reproductive problems.

This consensus paper focuses on grouping diagnostic hysteroscopic findings, structuring their reporting, and adopting standardized terminology for women with reproductive disorders. The virtual Nominal Group Technique, a structured consensus-building method, was adopted to ensure equal contribution from all members in the development of the final consensus.

The document provides a structured reporting of hysteroscopic findings into five sections, each systematically capturing patient characteristics, procedural findings, and pathological observations as follows: patient's characteristics, and findings from the vagina, cervix, uterine cavity, endometrium, and tubal ostia.

The inclusion of a finding in this structured report is not a proof of its clinical significance, but it could be used as a validation tool for further research.

The standardized reporting of hysteroscopic findings promotes consistent data collection across centers and could help inform research and exchange of clinical experience, enhancing the value of hysteroscopy in fertility evaluation.

title: Transperineal contrast-enhanced ultrasound: a rapid and reliable tool for differentiating abscesses from inflammatory masses in perianal Crohn's disease.
abstract: Background and aim Perianal abscesses are serious complications of Crohn's disease (CD) requiring timely and accurate diagnosis. Contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS), which in abdominal intestinal ultrasound (IUS) has shown diagnostic performance comparable to CT/MRI in distinguishing intra-abdominal abscesses from inflammatory masses, has not been systematically evaluated in the transperineal assessment of perianal Crohn's disease. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance, inter- and intra-observer agreement, and diagnostic confidence of transperineal CEUS versus conventional B-mode TPUS in CD patients with perianal symptoms and suspected septic complications. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 52 examinations of 37 adult CD patients presenting with painful perianal symptoms and suspected septic complications. Patients were included if TPUS detected lesions > 10 mm requiring CEUS characterization. Exclusion criteria were CEUS contraindications, simple fistulas, or large (>3 cm) obvious abscesses. All examinations were recorded, and three blinded experts independently assessed anonymized videos in random order. Lesions were classified as abscesses, inflammatory masses, or phlegmons. Agreement for lesion size, fluid content, and final diagnosis was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and Fleiss-Cohen's kappa (κ). Diagnostic confidence was assessed using a 5-point Likert scale. Results On B-mode, 17 abscesses, 32 inflammatory masses, and 3 phlegmons were identified. CEUS reclassified several, yielding 16 abscesses, 31 inflammatory masses, and 5 phlegmons. Of the 17 abscesses diagnosed on B-mode, only 4 were also classified as abscesses on CEUS, while 13 were reclassified; conversely, 11 inflammatory masses were reclassified as abscesses. Intra-observer reliability improved from κ = 0.55 with B-mode to κ = 0.95 with CEUS. Inter-observer agreement for diagnosis was poor with B-mode (κ = 0.31) but excellent with CEUS (κ = 0.83). Conclusions Transperineal CEUS significantly improves inter- and intra-observer agreement and diagnostic confidence compared with conventional B-mode TPUS when differentiating perianal abscesses from inflammatory masses/phlegmons in CD and frequently leads to lesion reclassification in clinically ambiguous cases.

title: Multi-modal ensemble learning prediction of anti-TNF treatment response in pediatric patients with Crohn's disease using clinical, radiomic, and deep learning MR enterography features.
abstract: Background Anti-tumor necrosis factor (TNF) medical therapy is a major advancement for Crohn's disease (CD) management, yet many patients fail to respond. This study aims to develop and evaluate a multi-modal ensemble model to predict anti-TNF treatment response in pediatric patients with CD using pre-treatment magnetic resonance enterography (MRE) and non-imaging clinical data. Methods This retrospective study included 92 pediatric CD patients (median [IQR] age, 14.6 [12.7, 16.6] years; 65.2% male; 37 responders and 55 non-responders) who underwent MRE within 3 months before initiating anti-TNF therapy between 2009 and 2021. Responders achieved mucosal healing within 36 months; non-responders did not, underwent surgery, or changed therapy. Four pre-treatment feature sets were used: (1) radiologist MRE assessment, (2) radiomic features from bowel regions, (3) deep learning features from representative bowel images, and (4) non-imaging clinical features. A 2-stage stacking ensemble model was trained and evaluated. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was the primary performance metric. Results The multi-modal ensemble model integrating all MRE-based features achieved an AUROC of 0.771 [95% confidence intervals (CI): 0.745, 0.797], outperforming models using individual feature types (radiologist assessment: 0.706 [0.691, 0.721]; radiomic: 0.710 [0.691, 0.729]; deep learning: 0.724 [0.700, 0.749]). Combining MRE and clinical features (0.739 [0.696, 0.781]) achieved the highest AUROC of 0.817 [0.793, 0.842], though not significantly (P = .10). Radiomic features reflecting intensity distribution and texture heterogeneity were most predictive of treatment response. Conclusion A multi-modal ensemble model combining MRE-based radiologist assessment, radiomic, deep learning, and clinical features accurately predicted anti-TNF treatment response in pediatric CD patients.

Four pre-treatment feature sets were used: (1) radiologist MRE assessment, (2) radiomic features from bowel regions, (3) deep learning features from representative bowel images, and (4) non-imaging clinical features. A 2-stage stacking ensemble model was trained and evaluated. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was the primary performance metric.

Results

The multi-modal ensemble model integrating all MRE-based features achieved an AUROC of 0.771 [95% confidence intervals (CI): 0.745, 0.797], outperforming models using individual feature types (radiologist assessment: 0.706 [0.691, 0.721]; radiomic: 0.710 [0.691, 0.729]; deep learning: 0.724 [0.700, 0.749]). Combining MRE and clinical features (0.739 [0.696, 0.781]) achieved the highest AUROC of 0.817 [0.793, 0.842], though not significantly (P = .10). Radiomic features reflecting intensity distribution and texture heterogeneity were most predictive of treatment response.

Conclusion

A multi-modal ensemble model combining MRE-based radiologist assessment, radiomic, deep learning, and clinical features accurately predicted anti-TNF treatment response in pediatric CD patients.

title: Endoscopic and histologic healing distribution and persistent rectosigmoiditis in moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis.
abstract: Background Mucosal healing in ulcerative colitis (UC) is believed to follow a proximal-to-distal pattern. We evaluated colonic healing distribution in patients with moderate-to-severe UC receiving adalimumab. Methods Patients from the SERENE UC (Study of a Novel Approach to Induction and Maintenance Dosing with Adalimumab in Patients with Moderate to Severe Ulcerative Colitis) trial with full colonoscopies and segmental biopsies at screening, weeks 8, and 52 were included for endoscopic and histologic analyses if baseline Mayo endoscopic subscore (MES) or Robarts Histopathology Index (RHI) score, respectively, was >0 in the ascending, transverse, and/or descending colon. Data were analyzed using a mixed model for repeated measures to account for clustering of segments within a patient. Results Endoscopic and histologic analyses comprised 76 and 79 patients, respectively. Score reductions were significantly greater vs the rectum in the ascending (week 8: MES, mean -0.78 [95% confidence interval (CI), -1.03 to -0.52]; RHI, mean -4.70 [95% CI, -6.92 to -2.49]; week 52: MES, mean -0.63 [95% CI, -0.91 to -0.35]; RHI, mean -2.39 [95% CI, -4.64 to -0.15]), transverse (week 8: MES, mean -0.69 [95% CI, -0.94 to -0.43]; RHI, mean -3.57 [95% CI, -5.62 to -1.51]; week 52: MES, mean -0.64 [95% CI, -0.89 to -0.38]; RHI, mean -2.88 [95% CI, -4.99 to -0.77]), and descending colon (week 8: MES, mean -0.40 [95% CI, -0.67 to -0.13]; RHI, mean -2.55 [95% CI, -4.94 to -0.16]; week 52: MES, mean -0.52 [95% CI, -0.70 to -0.34]; RHI, mean -3.47 [95% CI, -5.37 to -1.56]). Endoscopic improvement/remission and histologic remission were significantly more likely in the ascending and transverse colon than the rectum. Conclusions Our findings demonstrate that endoscopic and histologic healing is more challenging in the rectum compared with proximal colonic segments.

title: Stenosis of a novel frozen elephant trunk in a patient with chronic dissection.
abstract: A partial elephant trunk (PET), a new type of frozen elephant trunk, was designed to prevent distal stent graft-induced new entry using a thinner nitinol wire with less radial force. We report a case of PET stenosis in chronic dissection. Total arch replacement was performed using a PET. After weaning from cardiopulmonary bypass, the lower-limb blood pressure decreased to 90% of the upper-limb blood pressure. Intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography revealed incomplete PET expansion, and on postoperative day 1, the lower-to-upper body blood pressure ratio further decreased to 70% due to PET stenosis at the steeply angulated arch. Emergency thoracic endovascular aortic repair was successfully performed, completely resolving the pressure gradient.

title: Long-term Outcomes in Previously Healthy non-HIV Individuals with Cryptococcal Meningitis Treated with Pulse-taper Corticosteroids for Post-infectious Inflammatory Syndrome.
abstract: Background Post-infectious inflammatory response syndrome (PIIRS) is an increasingly recognized complication of cryptococcal meningoencephalitis (CM) in non-HIV infected hosts with significant morbidity and mortality. Data describing long-term outcomes following immunomodulatory therapy are limited. Methods We conducted a prospective observational study of 15 immunocompetent adults with CM-PIIRS treated with a pulse corticosteroid taper (PCT) regimen. Performance status, neurocognitive, ophthalmologic, audiologic, and radiologic assessments were performed at greater than one year following CM diagnosis. Results After one year, performance status continued to improve from both baseline and the post-pulse periods. Neurocognitive testing revealed mild residual deficits, within the limits of normal, most prominently in information processing and psychomotor speed. Ocular abnormalities were frequent at baseline but showed substantial and sustained reductions following PCT, particularly in retinal nerve fiber layer thickness. Visual field deficits improved by 40% and remained stable thereafter. Evidence for changes in hearing sensitivity at post 1-year follow-up was mixed with 44.5% of ears meeting criteria for improvement, 11% for worsening, and 44.5% being stable. Radiologic abnormalities improved in 79% of patients, although intermittent inflammatory flares occurred during PCT but responded to dose escalation. A prolonged corticosteroid taper may be helpful, and MRI imaging can be used to evaluate response to taper. Conclusions In immunocompetent patients with CM-PIIRS, adjunctive corticosteroid therapy was associated with sustained improvement in neurologic, visual, and radiologic outcomes with mixed improvement in hearing after a year of therapy, with mild residual deficits.

title: Bridging healthcare gaps through public-private partnerships in Nigeria: a scoping review.
abstract: Nigeria's healthcare system faces several persistent structural challenges. Public-private partnerships (PPPs) have emerged as a strategy to address these gaps, although evidence on their implementation and impact remains fragmented. This scoping review mapped the implementation models, outcomes, challenges and future directions of PPPs in Nigeria's healthcare system, following the Arksey and O'Malley framework and PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Literature searches were conducted across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar and grey literature sources. Studies were screened using Rayyan, while eligibility was guided by the population-concept-context framework. Data were synthesized using descriptive and thematic analysis. Twenty-four studies were included, covering PPP applications across primary, secondary, tertiary and community healthcare systems. Identified models included service delivery, financing, infrastructure, supply chain and governance partnerships. The included evidence reported improvements in healthcare access, diagnostic capacity, immunization coverage, infrastructure development and system efficiency, particularly in tuberculosis diagnostics, radiology, dialysis and radiotherapy services. However, weak governance, poor stakeholder coordination, funding instability, affordability barriers and inequitable urban concentration of benefits persisted. Strengthening regulatory frameworks, sustainable financing, accountability and equitable access may enhance PPP implementation and enable appropriately governed PPPs to contribute to selected dimensions of healthcare access and service capacity relevant to universal health coverage in Nigeria.
